current_manifest_record.axiom_use: Choice-free: the construction and specialized trace uniqueness use only finite algebra and diagram operations.

citations.quote:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)$ be the base configuration of
[[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]], with $h=\frac{1}{4(n+1)}$ and
$q_j=((2j-n-1)h,0)$. Fix an index $i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$. The two adjacent
base points are

$$q_i=\bigl((2i-n-1)h,0\bigr),\qquad q_{i+1}=\bigl((2i+1-n)h,0\bigr),$$

their **midpoint** is $m_i:=(q_i+q_{i+1})/2=((2i-n)h,0)=q_i+(h,0)$, and their
**support disc** is the open disc

$$U_i:=\bigl\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\lVert w-m_i\rVert_2<\tfrac32h\bigr\}.$$

The support disc contains the two base points $q_i,q_{i+1}$, whose distance from
$m_i$ is $h$, and it contains no other base point: for $k<i$ one has
$\lVert q_k-m_i\rVert_2=(2(i-k)+1)h\ge 3h$ and for $k>i+1$ one has
$\lVert q_k-m_i\rVert_2=(2(k-i)-1)h\ge3h$, both exceeding $\tfrac32h$. Moreover
$U_i\subseteq D^\circ$, because every point of $U_i$ has norm at most
$\lVert m_i\rVert_2+\tfrac32h\le(n-2)h+\tfrac32h<(n+1)h<1$. Finally
$U_i\cap U_j=\varnothing$ whenever $|i-j|>1$, since then the midpoints are at
distance $2|i-j|h\ge4h>3h$, twice the radius.

**The positive half twist.** Define $\rho\colon I\to\mathbb R^2$, the
**anticlockwise diamond path**, by

$$\rho(t):=\begin{cases}\bigl(2th-h,\,-2th\bigr),&0\le t\le \tfrac12,\\[2pt] \bigl(2th-h,\,2th-2h\bigr),&\tfrac12\le t\le1.\end{cases}$$

Thus $\rho(0)=(-h,0)$, $\rho(\tfrac12)=(0,-h)$, $\rho(1)=(h,0)$, and $\rho$ is
continuous, piecewise linear, and satisfies $\lVert\rho(t)\rVert_2\le h$ for all
$t$ with $\rho(t)\neq0$ throughout. The **elementary half twist at $i$**, written
$\sigma_i$, is the tuple of motions

$$(\sigma_i)_i(t):=m_i+\rho(t),\qquad (\sigma_i)_{i+1}(t):=m_i-\rho(t),\qquad (\sigma_i)_k(t):=q_k\ \ (k\notin\{i,i+1\}).$$

It is a braid based at $Q$
([[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]],
[[def-continuous-map-top]]): the two moving points stay in $U_i$ and are
antipodal about $m_i$, so they are distinct; every other point is fixed and lies
outside $U_i$; and the endpoint permutation is the transposition of $i$ and
$i+1$, since $(\sigma_i)_i(1)=m_i+(h,0)=q_{i+1}$ and
$(\sigma_i)_{i+1}(1)=m_i-(h,0)=q_i$.

The words *positive* and *anticlockwise* refer to the fixed orientation of the
plane of the disc and to the fixed planar projection whose horizontal axis
contains $Q$: the moving pair turns through the half turn anticlockwise, the
label $i$ passing below its midpoint and the label $i+1$ above. Together with
the first-under-second stacking convention of
[[prop-stacking-of-geometric-braids-is-well-defined]] this fixes the sign
convention for every signed crossing on this page and its companion.

**The opposite half twist.** The **opposite** (clockwise) half twist at $i$ is
defined by the reflected path

$$\rho^{-}(t):=\bigl(\rho_1(t),-\rho_2(t)\bigr),$$

through the motions $(\sigma_i^{-})_i(t):=m_i+\rho^{-}(t)$,
$(\sigma_i^{-})_{i+1}(t):=m_i-\rho^{-}(t)$ and
$(\sigma_i^{-})_k(t):=q_k$ for $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$. It is again a braid supported
in $U_i$ with endpoint permutation the transposition of $i$ and $i+1$; its pair
turns through the same half turn clockwise, the label $i$ passing above the
midpoint. The two motions are not equal, and they are not related by a
reparametrisation of the height: they are the two signed crossings of the pair.

**The opposite motion is the group inverse.** For a braid $\beta$ the reversed
braid $\overline\beta_j(t)=z_{\pi(\beta)^{-1}(j)}(1-t)$ represents
$[\beta]^{-1}$ in the group $G_n$
([[thm-geometric-braids-form-a-group]]). For $\beta=\sigma_i$ one computes
$\overline{\sigma_i}=\sigma_i^{-}$: reversing the height and relabelling by the
transposition of $i$ and $i+1$ sends $\rho(t)=m_i+(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ to the
motion with relative path $-\rho(1-t)$, which is the reflected path
$\rho^-$ traversed from $t=0$ to $t=1$. Hence

$$[\sigma_i^{-}]=[\sigma_i]^{-1}\qquad\text{in }G_n .$$

**Elementary cases.** For $n\le1$ there is no index $i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$,
and there are no elementary half twists; the assertions above are vacuous. For
$n\ge2$ and $1\le i\le n-1$ both $[\sigma_i]$ and $[\sigma_i^{-}]$ are
nonidentity elements of $G_n$, since their endpoint permutations are
transpositions, which are not the identity permutation.

**Two letters do not commute in general.** For adjacent indices the supports
$U_i$ and $U_{i+1}$ overlap and no commutation is asserted;
[[lem-geometric-far-commutativity]] proves commutativity only for disjoint
supports.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

Fix $n\ge0$, a commutative ring $R$, and $\delta\in R$. For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ be the elementary cup-cap diagram of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. Then

$$d_i^2=\delta d_i\ (1\le i<n),\qquad d_i d_{i+1}d_i=d_i,\quad d_{i+1}d_i d_{i+1}=d_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\qquad d_i d_j=d_jd_i\ (1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Consequently the assignment $u_i\mapsto d_i$ extends to a unital $R$-algebra homomorphism

$$\pi_n:P_n(R,\delta)\longrightarrow\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\delta\in R$, and use the noncrossing-pairing diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], with the left factor stacked above the right factor. For a basis diagram $D:n\to n$, close each top endpoint to the corresponding bottom endpoint outside the rectangle and let $c(D)$ be the number of circles in the resulting finite graph. Define

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$$

and extend $R$-linearly to $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. This is the **unnormalized closure trace**. In particular, $\operatorname{Tr}_0(1_0)=1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_n(1_n)=\delta^n$. No unit or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is required.

Let $\cup:0\to2$ and $\cap:2\to0$ be the standard cup and cap in the diagram category. For $n\ge1$ define the **right partial trace** by

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(x)=(1_{n-1}\otimes\cap)\circ(x\otimes1_1)\circ(1_{n-1}\otimes\cup),\qquad x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

It is a map $\mathrm{TL}_n\to\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$. If $\delta$ is a unit, define $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. This agrees with the normalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] over $\mathbb C$ when $\delta\ne0$.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the Laurent polynomial ring and let
$\Lambda:=A[z]=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ be the polynomial ring over $A$ in one
indeterminate ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]). For $n\ge1$ let
$H(n):=\Lambda\otimes_AH_v(n)$ be the scalar extension of the generic type-A
Hecke algebra of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), so that $H(n)$ is the unital
$\Lambda$-algebra with generators $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ subject to
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v,\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1},\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$
and $H(1)=\Lambda$. The $\Lambda$-algebra $H(n)$ is free with basis
$\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$, where $T_w$ is the product of the generators along a reduced
word ([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]],
[[def-symmetric-group]]).

The generators induce a $\Lambda$-algebra homomorphism
$\iota_n:H(n)\to H(n+1)$, $T_i\mapsto T_i$; it is injective, so we identify
$H(n)$ with its image, a $\Lambda$-subalgebra of $H(n+1)$.

A **Markov trace on the type-A Hecke tower** is a family of $\Lambda$-linear
maps $\operatorname{tr}_n:H(n)\to\Lambda$, $n\ge1$, such that

- (M1) $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$ for one (equivalently, by (M2), every) $n$;
- (M2) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}\circ\iota_n=\operatorname{tr}_n$ for all $n\ge1$;
- (M3) $\operatorname{tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{tr}_n(yx)$ for all $x,y\in H(n)$;
- (M4) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(x\,T_n)=z\,\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$ for all $n\ge1$
  and $x\in H(n)$.

Here $z\in\Lambda$ is a formal parameter, distinct from the Hecke parameter $v$;
no value of $z$ is fixed or inverted by this definition, and the trace takes
values in $\Lambda$, not in a field.

**Caveats.** This is a family over the whole tower, not a single functional; the
conditions (M1)--(M4) are a definition, so no trace is asserted to exist here
(existence and uniqueness is
[[thm-the-ocneanu-markov-trace-exists-and-is-unique]]). By (M3), (M4) is
equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(u\,T_n\,v)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(uv)$ for
all $u,v\in H(n)$: applied to $uT_nv$ one gets
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(uT_nv)=\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(T_nvu)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(vu)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(uv)$,
and conversely take $v=1$.

Let $H(1)\subset H(2)\subset\cdots$ be the type-A Hecke tower over
$\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of [[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]].
Then there exists a unique Markov trace $(\operatorname{tr}_n)_{n\ge1}$ on this
tower in the sense of [[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]]. Moreover
it satisfies, for all $n\ge1$, all $x,y\in H(n)$ and all $1\le i\le n-1$:

- (a) $\operatorname{tr}_n(T_i)=z$;
- (b) $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_ny)=z\,\operatorname{tr}_n(xy)$;
- (c) $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is determined by (M1)--(M4) alone; it takes values in
  $\Lambda$ and is computed by iterating (b) along the free basis of
  [[lem-the-hecke-tower-is-free-over-the-previous-level]].

Let $H(n)$ be the Hecke tower over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]]. Then: (1) the elements
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ are units of $H(n)$ with
$T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$; (2) the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$
descends to a group homomorphism
$$\pi_n:B_n\longrightarrow H(n)^{\times},\qquad \pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i,$$
where $H(n)^{\times}$ is the group of units of $H(n)$; (3) for every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$\pi_n(\beta)=T_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots T_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$, and
$\pi_{n+1}(\iota_n^{\mathrm{Br}}(\beta))=\iota_n(\pi_n(\beta))$ for all
$\beta\in B_n$ under the standard inclusion of braid groups $B_n\to B_{n+1}$.

Let $H(1)\subset H(2)\subset\cdots$ be the Hecke tower of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]], with $H(n)$ free of rank $n!$
over $\Lambda$ with basis $\{T_w:w\in S_n\}$
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]), and for
$1\le i\le n$ put $w^{(i)}:=s_ns_{n-1}\cdots s_{n-i+1}$, $w^{(0)}:=1$. Then for
every $n\ge1$:

1. $H(n+1)$ is a free left $H(n)$-module with basis
   $T_{w^{(0)}},T_{w^{(1)}},\dots,T_{w^{(n)}}$: every element of $H(n+1)$ has a
   unique expression $\sum_{i=0}^{n}x_iT_{w^{(i)}}$ with $x_i\in H(n)$;
2. $H(n+1)$ is also a free right $H(n)$-module with basis
   $T_{(w^{(0)})^{-1}},T_{(w^{(1)})^{-1}},\dots,T_{(w^{(n)})^{-1}}$;
3. the  $H(n)$-sub-bimodule $H(n)T_nH(n)$ equals the direct sum
   $\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}H(n)T_{w^{(i)}}$, and the multiplication map
   $$H(n)\otimes_{H(n-1)}H(n)\longrightarrow H(n+1),\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto xT_ny,$$
   is an isomorphism of $H(n)$-bimodules onto $H(n)T_nH(n)$; consequently
   $H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus H(n)T_nH(n)$ holds as a direct sum of $H(n)$-bimodules in
   the form $H(n+1)=H(n)\oplus\bigl(H(n)\otimes_{H(n-1)}H(n)\bigr)$. All three parts are proved here. Each chosen nonidentity minimal left-coset representative $w^{(i)}$
   has a displayed reduced expression containing $s_n$ exactly once; this does
   not characterize all basis elements whose reduced expressions contain
   $s_n$ once. In the tensor notation of part (3), set $H(0):=\Lambda$, the
   scalar extension $\Lambda\otimes_AH_v(0)$, so the $n=1$ case is defined.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic

derivations.claim: Use source coordinates $(u,v)$ with their standard positive orientation and positive projection coordinates $(t,x)$ on the braid box. For $h>0$, the map $(t,x)=(v,-2hu)$ has determinant $2h>0$. It sends the source over direction $(1,1)$ to $(1,-2h)$ and the source under direction $(-1,1)$ to $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is $4h>0$. The source left/right pairs have constant $u$, hence constant braid position $x$ and give the through pairing $I$; the source top/bottom pairs have constant $v$, hence constant braid time $t$ and give the cup-cap $e_i$. The displayed page coordinates $(x,t)$ reverse the positive projection orientation; their visual quarter-turn is not the orientation comparison. Thus its two smoothings are $I$ with weight $A$ and $e_i$ with weight $A^{-1}$. For the opposite crossing the pairings exchange. Hence the local operators are $$C_i=AI+A^{-1}e_i,\qquad C_i^{-}=A^{-1}I+Ae_i.$$ The relations [F5] and [F6] show these operators satisfy the Artin relations and are mutual inverses; distant generators commute by [F5].

Define $\rho_n(\sigma_i)=C_i$ and $S_i:=-A^{-1}C_i=-I-qe_i$. With $t=q^2$ and $\delta=-(q+q^{-1})$, direct multiplication gives $$S_i^2=I+(2q+q^2\delta)e_i=I+(q-q^3)e_i =(t-1)S_i+t.$$ The braid and distant-commutation relations for $S_i$ follow from [F5] and step 1.1. Under the coefficient map $\psi:\Lambda\to R_A$ given by $v\mapsto t$ and $z\mapsto z_0$, the assignment $T_i\mapsto S_i$ therefore defines a compatible homomorphism $\rho_H$ from the specialized Hecke tower to the Temperley--Lieb diagram algebras. For a braid word, this map sends $\pi_n(\beta)$ to the product of the corresponding $S_i^{\pm1}$.

The element $A^{-4}+1$ is a unit in $R_A$ and $\delta=-A^2(A^{-4}+1)$ is therefore a unit. Set $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. By [F7], $\tau_n(1)=1$, $\tau_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\tau_n(x)$, and $\tau_n$ is cyclic. Since $S_n=-I-qe_n$, the last closure rule of [F7] gives $$\tau_{n+1}((x\otimes1)S_n) =-\tau_n(x)-q\delta^{-1}\tau_n(x) =-\frac{1}{q^2+1}\tau_n(x)=z_0\tau_n(x).$$ Thus $\tau\circ\rho_H$ satisfies all specialized Markov-trace rules, where $\rho_H(T_i)=S_i$.

The decomposition in [F10] is a direct sum of modules spanned by disjoint subsets of the Hecke standard basis. Under $\psi$, that basis remains a basis, so for $H_\psi(n):=H(n)\otimes_{\Lambda,\psi}R_A$ the specialized tower still has $H_\psi(n+1)=H_\psi(n)\oplus H_\psi(n)T_nH_\psi(n)$. Any specialized Markov trace is therefore determined by its restriction to $H_\psi(n)$: restriction determines the first summand, while cyclicity and the Markov rule force $\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_ny)=z_0\operatorname{tr}_n(yx)$ on every product in the second summand. Starting at $H(1)$, induction proves uniqueness, without dividing by any specialized parameter. The scalar extension of the Ocneanu trace exists by [F8], so the trace in step 3.1 equals that specialized trace.

Expand each crossing of $\beta$ by $C_i$ or $C_i^{-}$ and close the resulting Temperley–Lieb diagrams. The unnormalized trace counts each closed state circle with a factor $\delta$, whereas the bracket state sum counts it with $\delta^{|S|-1}$; hence $$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_n(\rho_n(\beta)) =\delta^{n-1}\tau_n(\rho_n(\beta)).$$ Since $C_i=-A S_i$ and $C_i^{-}=(-A)^{-1}S_i^{-1}$, multiplying along an Artin word gives $\rho_n(\beta)=(-A)^{e(\beta)}\rho_H(\pi_n(\beta))$. Step 4.1 now gives the displayed trace identity.

The closure of the identity in $B_1$ has one circle; the state sum gives $\delta^{1-1}=1$, and its trace expression gives $\delta^0(-A)^0\operatorname{tr}_1(1)=1$. For positive stabilization, the Markov trace factor is $z_0=-1/(q^2+1)$, so the bracket formula changes by $$(-A)\delta z_0=-A^3.$$ For negative stabilization, [F9] and [F8] give trace factor $$z_-:=t^{-1}(z_0+1-t)=-\frac{q^2}{q^2+1};$$ the bracket formula changes by $$\delta(-A)^{-1}z_-=-A^{-3}.$$ This proves the unknot value and both stabilization normalizations.

citations.quote:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

For every commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and objects $m,n,p,q\ge0$, the raw diagram data of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]] form a strict monoidal category $\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)$ with hom-modules $M_R(m,n)$ and the stated $R$-bilinear stacking composition. Composition is associative, the identity diagrams are two-sided identities, and horizontal juxtaposition is a strict monoidal bifunctor with unit object $0$. Consequently $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)}(n)=\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is a unital associative $R$-algebra whose underlying $R$-module is free on its noncrossing pairing diagrams.

Fix $n\ge0$, a commutative ring $R$, and $\delta\in R$. For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ be the elementary cup-cap diagram of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. Then

$$d_i^2=\delta d_i\ (1\le i<n),\qquad d_i d_{i+1}d_i=d_i,\quad d_{i+1}d_i d_{i+1}=d_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\qquad d_i d_j=d_jd_i\ (1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Consequently the assignment $u_i\mapsto d_i$ extends to a unital $R$-algebra homomorphism

$$\pi_n:P_n(R,\delta)\longrightarrow\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements of
a regular oriented link diagram ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]),
performed inside a small closed disk while the diagram outside the disk is left
unchanged, and understood up to planar isotopy outside the disk
([[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]). All sign and orientation variants of
each local picture are included.

**(R1) Kink creation and deletion.** A single strand is replaced by a small
kink: two arcs crossing once and otherwise disjoint from the strand, with the
over/under datum of the new crossing as in the picture. The move is allowed in
both directions (create or delete the kink) and with both signs of the kink,
the sign being the sign of the crossing created. The orientations of the two
strands of the kink are the two possible consistent orientations through the
crossing, and all of them occur in the move list.

**(R2) Slide of two strands.** Two local arcs belonging to two strands are
replaced so that the number of crossings between those strands changes by two
of opposite signs: the standard picture slides one strand over or under the
other, creating or deleting the pair of crossings, with the two crossings being
the two possible signs in either order. All four orientation patterns of the
two strands at the two crossings are included.

**(R3) Sliding a strand past a crossing.** One strand is moved across an
existing crossing of two other strands, so that the crossing of the two other
strands passes from one side of the moving strand to the other; the three
crossings of the local picture keep their signs and the over/under data are
preserved. The three strands must have a consistent strict height order:
one is above both others, one below both, and the remaining strand is between
them. The cyclic over/under pattern is excluded. Every orientation pattern
and all six height orders of this standard local picture are included.

A local R2 or R3 picture is **braid-like** when, after a local coordinate
change and deformation, all participating strands run in the same positive
longitudinal direction. This is a local condition and does not require a
globally chosen braid axis. R1 is kept as a separate kink move.

The strands keep their orientations throughout every move. The union of the
three move types, together with planar isotopy, generates the equivalence
relation on diagrams used in the Reidemeister equivalence theorem below; the
moves are sometimes called R1, R2, R3 as above. Since every move changes the
diagram only inside a disk, it has a type and a finite list of local
orientation/sign variants, and each variant is realized by an ambient isotopy
as the next items show. The complete list of variants is required because the
Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams and count
signed crossings.

derivations.claim: Use source coordinates $(u,v)$ with their standard positive orientation and positive projection coordinates $(t,x)$ on the braid box. For $h>0$, the map $(t,x)=(v,-2hu)$ has determinant $2h>0$. It sends the source over direction $(1,1)$ to $(1,-2h)$ and the source under direction $(-1,1)$ to $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is $4h>0$. The source left/right pairs have constant $u$, hence constant braid position $x$ and give the through pairing $I$; the source top/bottom pairs have constant $v$, hence constant braid time $t$ and give the cup-cap $e_i$. The displayed page coordinates $(x,t)$ reverse the positive projection orientation; their visual quarter-turn is not the orientation comparison. For the opposite crossing, rotating the source chart by a positive quarter-turn exchanges the two endpoint pairings, so its A/B smoothings are respectively $e_i$ and $I$. By [F1] these expansions are $C_i=AI+A^{-1}e_i$ and $C_i^{-}=A^{-1}I+Ae_i$. Using [F2] and [F3], $$C_iC_i^{-}=(AI+A^{-1}e_i)(A^{-1}I+Ae_i)=I+(A^2+A^{-2}+\delta)e_i=I.$$ The same multiplication in the other order gives $C_i^{-}C_i=I$, since both factors are polynomials in $e_i$. Thus the two opposite crossings in an R2 pair cancel in either order.

Put $x=e_i$ and $y=e_{i+1}$. Expanding and using [F3] gives $$C_iC_{i+1}C_i=A^3I+A(2x+y)+A^{-1}(xy+yx+\delta x)+A^{-3}x,$$ while interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives $$C_{i+1}C_iC_{i+1}=A^3I+A(2y+x)+A^{-1}(yx+xy+\delta y)+A^{-3}y.$$ Their difference is $A^{-1}(A^2+\delta+A^{-2})(x-y)=0$. Hence the two sides of the braid-like R3 move have equal bracket operators.

Near the three-strand event, choose a linear longitudinal coordinate nonzero on each of the three tangent lines, shrink the event disk, and orient the unoriented local tracks in its increasing direction. All three tracks are then monotone; these temporary arrows do not affect the bracket. Label the tracks $1,2,3$ at the incoming end. The two R3 sides meet their pairs in orders $(12,13,23)$ and $(23,13,12)$, and a strict height order permits exactly the exponent triples $+++, --- , ++-, -++, +--, --+$. The triples $+-+$ and $-+-$ would require a cyclic height order. Put $a=C_i$ and $b=C_{i+1}$. Besides $aba=bab$ from step 1.2 and its inverse from step 1.1, the four needed identities are $$ab a^{-1}=b^{-1}ab,\qquad a^{-1}ba=bab^{-1},\qquad ab^{-1}a^{-1}=b^{-1}a^{-1}b,\qquad a^{-1}b^{-1}a=ba^{-1}b^{-1}.$$ The first follows by multiplying $aba=bab$ on the left by $b^{-1}$ and on the right by $a^{-1}$; the second follows by multiplying on the left by $a^{-1}$ and on the right by $b^{-1}$; the last two are their inverses. Thus each of the six height orders gives equality with exactly its actual over/under choices. For R2, choose a longitudinal coordinate along the common tangent at the bigon event, shrink the disk, and temporarily orient both tracks increasingly; the two local crossings have opposite types and cancel by step 1.1. Reversing any original strand arrow leaves all smoothing weights unchanged. Adjoining the unchanged exterior tangle and closing its boundary preserves these equalities: expand each crossing into its two smoothings, use bilinearity, and evaluate each resulting crossingless closed diagram with one factor $\delta$ per circle as in [F2]. This gives equal sums $\sum_S A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|}$ on the two sides. Every complete smoothing of the nonempty diagram has $|S|\ge1$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ is nonzero in the integral domain $\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$; hence these sums are $\delta\langle D\rangle$ and $\delta\langle D'\rangle$. Cancelling $\delta$ proves $\langle D\rangle=\langle D'\rangle$, so every R2/R3 variant preserves the bracket.

current_manifest_record.statement:
**Input and output.** The input is one finite ASCII string. Its prescribed form is
`n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of
the form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is
no whitespace or trailing character. The output is either the rejection symbol
`REJECT` or an element of the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and
$d=\delta$.

1. **Parse and validate.** If the input is not in the stated syntax, if
   $\ell$ is not the number of letter tokens, if $n=0$, or if any token index
   fails $1\le i<n$, return `REJECT` and halt. Otherwise read the tokens as the
   finite signed Artin word
   $$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}, \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.$$

2. **Compute the closure data.** Form the BMW product
   $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}$.
   Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles,
   including fixed points, of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ of
   $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

3. **Enumerate a matching basis.** Work in the unit rectangle with top and
   bottom endpoints at $(j/(n+1),1)$ and $(j/(n+1),0)$, respectively, for
   $1\le j\le n$. Fix a prefix-free binary encoding of finite rational
   polygonal diagrams with over/under data, with rational coordinates written
   as reduced numerator/positive-denominator pairs. Number the tangle endpoints in cyclic order
   $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. Enumerate perfect matchings
   recursively: pair the least unmatched endpoint with each greater unmatched
   endpoint in increasing order, then continue on the remaining endpoints. For
   each matching $\mu$, scan finite diagram codes in increasing code length and
   then lexicographically. Choose the first code of a rational polygonal tangle
   diagram with that connector, no closed component and no strand self-crossing,
   in which the open strands are oriented from their lower-numbered to their
   higher-numbered endpoint, ordered by initial endpoint, and every crossing is
   over on the first traversed strand. This is the standard descending
   representative $T_\mu$. Give each polygonal segment its distinct code label
   and its orientation inherited from its strand. The standard descending
   matching spanning lemma guarantees that such codes exist and that they all
   represent the same tangle class for each $\mu$.

4. **Build generator matrices by skein reduction.** For every signed generator
   $g_i^{\pm1}$, form its left-multiplication matrix in the ordered basis
   $\{T_\mu\}$. The column at $T_\mu$ is computed by reducing
   $g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the
   smaller to the larger endpoint label and order them by their initial
   endpoints. Order each closed component by the least label of its polygonal
   segments, start at the initial end of that segment, and follow its stored
   orientation. Traverse the strands in that order and select the first
   crossing whose first encountered branch is under. Segment labels are
   retained through crossing switches and smoothings. Let $R(D)$ denote the
   coordinate vector of the current tangle expression in the matching basis.
   If the selected crossing is $D_+$ in the fixed chart, put $\eta=1$; if it
   is $D_-$, put $\eta=-1$. Replace
   $$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr),$$
   using the fixed through smoothing $D_0$ and cup-cap smoothing $D_\infty$.
   Recurse on all three resulting terms. The switched branch has one fewer
   non-descending crossing and each smoothing has one fewer crossing. At a
   descending tangle leaf, use the traversal to lift each already traversed
   segment over the remaining diagram, removing self-crossings while fixing
   the boundary; retain crossings between distinct open strands in their
   ordered layers. Remove the resulting framing curls with factors $a$ or
   $a^{-1}$ and each closed component with factor $d$. Record the remaining
   standard matching tangle and add its coefficient to that matching coordinate.

5. **Apply the matrices and evaluate the trace row.** Start with the coordinate
   vector of the identity tangle and apply the generator matrices from the
   rightmost braid letter to the leftmost, obtaining $v_\beta$, the coordinate
   vector of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$. For each matching $\mu$, close $T_\mu$ by the
   first code in the same finite-code order for pairwise disjoint rational
   polygonal arcs outside the rectangle joining corresponding top and bottom
   endpoints without a twist. Orient each such arc from its smaller to larger
   cyclic endpoint label. Evaluate this closed diagram by the same deterministic
   traversal and skein recursion: at a descending leaf, straighten the
   traversal-ordered components, remove their framing curls with factors
   $a,a^{-1}$, remove each free circle with factor $d$, and use
   $P(\varnothing)=1$ for the empty diagram. Set
   $$t_\mu=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_\mu}),\qquad \tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta.$$

6. **Return**
   $$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$
   All matrices and recursion trees are finite, all coefficients lie in $T$,
   and no division by the skein variable is used.

citations.quote:
Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

For each integer $n\ge0$, let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with $z_D=q-q^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra formed from regular-isotopy classes with crossing rule $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, and free-circle factor $d$, where $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. Number its $2n$ boundary endpoints in cyclic order as $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. A connector is a perfect matching of these endpoints. Orient each open strand from its lower-numbered endpoint to its higher-numbered endpoint and order the open strands by their initial endpoints. Place the finitely many closed strands after the open strands in any fixed order, with a chosen orientation and initial point for each. A diagram is totally descending if, in this traversal order, the first branch encountered at each crossing is the overpassing branch. Then $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ is spanned by one loop-free, self-crossing-free totally descending tangle for each connector. These representatives can have crossings between distinct strands; their crossing data are fixed by the total traversal order. For $n=0$ the single representative is the empty tangle, and for $n=1$ it is the straight strand.

Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and let $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. For each $n\ge0$, index the standard descending matching tangles by the perfect matchings $m$ of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. Reflect a second such tangle across the horizontal midline and glue corresponding boundary endpoints to obtain a closed diagram. Let $M_n$ be the matrix whose $(m,m')$ entry is the scalar Dubrovnik evaluation $P$ of this closure. Then $\det M_n$ is nonzero in $S$, its image is a non-zero-divisor in $T$, and the standard matching tangles are linearly independent over $T$. The assertion is over this universal coefficient extension and makes no independence claim after an arbitrary nonflat specialization.

For $n\ge1$, let $\Phi_n$ be the BMW-to-Dubrovnik tangle homomorphism over $T$, let $\widehat{t}$ denote closure of an $(n,n)$ tangle by joining corresponding top and bottom endpoints without a twist, and define
$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$
Then $\tau_n$ is a cyclic $T$-linear trace, compatible with the tower inclusion $\iota_n:BMW_n\to BMW_{n+1}$ that adds one straight strand, and for every $x\in BMW_n$,
$$\tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x))=\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n)=a d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)e_n)=d^{-1}\tau_n(x),$$
where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.

Put $A=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},s,d^{\pm1}]/(s(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$. This ring is an integral domain and embeds in $\mathbb Q(i)(a,s)$ by $d\mapsto1+(a-a^{-1})/s$, where $i^2=-1$. A link diagram means a finite generic immersion of circles in the oriented plane with over/under data at its double points. Regular isotopy is generated by planar isotopy and Reidemeister moves II and III. A positive curl is a one-crossing curl whose oriented self-crossing has sign $+1$; its sign is independent of the direction chosen on its component. There is a unique function $P$ from link diagrams, including the empty diagram, to $A$ with $P(\varnothing)=1$, unchanged by regular isotopy, satisfying the following local rules: a positive or negative curl multiplies $P$ by $a$ or $a^{-1}$; a disjoint trivial circle multiplies $P$ by $d$; and $P(L_+)-P(L_-)=s(P(L_0)-P(L_\infty))$. Here in an oriented disk with four cyclically labelled endpoints $1,2,3,4$, $L_+$ connects $1$ to $3$ over the strand from $2$ to $4$, and the two smoothings are chosen so that the oriented smoothing for any orientation making this crossing positive is $L_0$; $L_-$ reverses the crossing and $L_\infty$ is the other smoothing. Rotating the disk interchanges both differences and preserves the rule. In particular the empty diagram freely generates the quotient of the free $A$-module on closed diagrams by these rules.

Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

current_manifest_record.title: The BMW braid-closure algorithm terminates and returns its stated value
current_manifest_record.statement:
For every finite ASCII input string, the BMW braid-closure algorithm parses the
form `n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of the
form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is no
whitespace or trailing character. It returns `REJECT` exactly when the string
fails this syntax, the parsed value of $\ell$ differs from the actual number of
letter tokens, the parsed strand count is $n=0$, or some letter index fails
$1\le i<n$. For every other input, the algorithm terminates after finitely
many basis-code searches, algebra operations, and skein reductions, and returns exactly
$$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta).$$
Here $w$ is the determinant writhe of the oriented closure, $c$ is its
component count, and $\tau_n$ is the normalized scalar closure trace. No
asymptotic complexity bound is asserted.

**Input and output.** The input is one finite ASCII string. Its prescribed form is
`n;ell;word`, where `n` and `ell` are canonical decimal natural numbers
(`0`, or a nonzero decimal digit followed by zero or more decimal digits), and
`word` is empty if $\ell=0$ or is exactly $\ell$ comma-separated tokens of
the form `i+` or `i-`, with `i` a canonical decimal natural number. There is
no whitespace or trailing character. The output is either the rejection symbol
`REJECT` or an element of the coefficient extension $T$ with $a=\rho$ and
$d=\delta$.

1. **Parse and validate.** If the input is not in the stated syntax, if
   $\ell$ is not the number of letter tokens, if $n=0$, or if any token index
   fails $1\le i<n$, return `REJECT` and halt. Otherwise read the tokens as the
   finite signed Artin word
   $$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}, \qquad \varepsilon_j\in\{-1,1\}.$$

2. **Compute the closure data.** Form the BMW product
   $b_\beta=g_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots g_{i_\ell}^{\varepsilon_\ell}$.
   Set $w=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\varepsilon_j$ and let $c$ be the number of cycles,
   including fixed points, of the permutation $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$ of
   $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

3. **Enumerate a matching basis.** Work in the unit rectangle $R=[0,1]^2$ with top and
   bottom endpoints at $(j/(n+1),1)$ and $(j/(n+1),0)$, respectively, for
   $1\le j\le n$. Fix a prefix-free binary encoding of finite rational
   polygonal diagrams with over/under data, with rational coordinates written
   as reduced numerator/positive-denominator pairs. Number the tangle endpoints in cyclic order
   $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. Enumerate perfect matchings
   recursively: pair the least unmatched endpoint with each greater unmatched
   endpoint in increasing order, then continue on the remaining endpoints. For
   each matching $\mu$, scan finite diagram codes in increasing code length and
   then lexicographically. Choose the first code of a rational polygonal tangle
   diagram with that connector, no closed component and no strand self-crossing,
   in which the open strands are oriented from their lower-numbered to their
   higher-numbered endpoint, ordered by initial endpoint, and every crossing is
   over on the first traversed strand. This is the standard descending
   representative $T_\mu$. Give each polygonal segment its distinct code label
   and its orientation inherited from its strand. The spanning lemma identifies the standard descending class for each connector.

4. **Build generator matrices by skein reduction.** For every signed generator
   $g_i^{\pm1}$, form its left-multiplication matrix in the ordered basis
   $\{T_\mu\}$. The column at $T_\mu$ is computed by reducing
   $g_i^{\pm1}T_\mu$. In each current diagram, orient open strands from the smaller to the larger endpoint
   label and order them by their initial endpoints. Order closed components by
   their least segment labels. In each closed component, start by traversing its
   least-labelled segment from its designated initial endpoint to its terminal
   endpoint; then follow the unique continuation of that component, traversing
   later segments in whichever direction reaches the next endpoint. At a crossing
   continue along the same strand, and after a smoothing continue along the
   prescribed pairing. Retain segment labels and their designated endpoints
   through switches and smoothings. This gives a deterministic traversal even
   when segment orientations do not join coherently around a closed component.
   Traverse the open strands followed by the closed components in this order,
   and select the first crossing whose first encountered branch is under. Let $R(D)$ denote the
   coordinate vector of the current tangle expression in the matching basis.
   If the selected crossing is $D_+$ in the fixed chart, put $\eta=1$; if it
   is $D_-$, put $\eta=-1$. Replace
   $$R(D)=R(D^{\mathrm{sw}})+\eta z_D\bigl(R(D_0)-R(D_\infty)\bigr),$$
   using the fixed through smoothing $D_0$ and cup-cap smoothing $D_\infty$.
   Recurse on all three resulting terms. The switched branch has one fewer
   non-descending crossing and each smoothing has one fewer crossing. At a
   descending tangle leaf, use the traversal to lift each already traversed
   segment over the remaining diagram, removing self-crossings while fixing
   the boundary; retain crossings between distinct open strands in their
   ordered layers. Remove the resulting framing curls with factors $a$ or
   $a^{-1}$ and each closed component with factor $d$. Record the remaining
   standard matching tangle and add its coefficient to that matching coordinate.

5. **Apply the matrices and evaluate the trace row.** Start with the coordinate
   vector of the identity tangle and apply the generator matrices from the
   rightmost braid letter to the leftmost, obtaining $v_\beta$, the coordinate
   vector of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$. For each matching $\mu$, close $T_\mu$ by the following fixed untwisted
   planar closure. For $1\le j\le n$ put $x_j=j/(n+1)$ and
   $\epsilon_j=1/(j+1)$, and add the rational polygonal arc

   $$C_j:(x_j,1)\to(x_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,1+\epsilon_j)\to(1+\epsilon_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,-\epsilon_j)\to(x_j,0).$$

   These arcs lie outside $R$ except at their specified endpoints and are
   pairwise disjoint: if $j<k$, then $x_j<x_k$ and $\epsilon_j>\epsilon_k$,
   so their exterior lanes are nested. Orient $C_j$ from top endpoint $j$ to
   bottom endpoint $\bar j$, give its segments fresh distinct labels, and use
   this same arc system for every matching. It represents the untwisted closure
   used in the definition of $\tau_n$. Evaluate the closed diagram by the
   deterministic traversal and skein recursion of Step 4: at a descending leaf,
   straighten the traversal-ordered components, remove their framing curls with
   factors $a,a^{-1}$, remove each free circle with factor $d$, and use
   $P(\varnothing)=1$ for the empty diagram.

   Set
   $$t_\mu=d^{-n}P(\widehat{T_\mu}),\qquad \tau_n(b_\beta)=t^{\mathsf T}v_\beta.$$

6. **Return**
   $$-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta).$$

$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$

where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.

Put $A=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},s,d^{\pm1}]/(s(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$. This ring is an integral domain and embeds in $\mathbb Q(i)(a,s)$ by $d\mapsto1+(a-a^{-1})/s$, where $i^2=-1$.
