For each integer $n\ge0$, let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$, with $z_D=q-q^{-1}$. Let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra formed from regular-isotopy classes with crossing rule $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$, curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, and free-circle factor $d$, where $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. Number its $2n$ boundary endpoints in cyclic order as $1,2,\ldots,n,\bar n,\ldots,\bar2,\bar1$. A connector is a perfect matching of these endpoints. Orient each open strand from its lower-numbered endpoint to its higher-numbered endpoint and order the open strands by their initial endpoints. Place the finitely many closed strands after the open strands in any fixed order, with a chosen orientation and initial point for each. A diagram is totally descending if, in this traversal order, the first branch encountered at each crossing is the overpassing branch. Then $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ is spanned by one loop-free, self-crossing-free totally descending tangle for each connector. These representatives can have crossings between distinct strands; their crossing data are fixed by the total traversal order. For $n=0$ the single representative is the empty tangle, and for $n=1$ it is the straight strand.

Let $S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$ and let $T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z)$. For each $n\ge0$, index the standard descending matching tangles by the perfect matchings $m$ of the $2n$ boundary endpoints. Reflect a second such tangle across the horizontal midline and glue corresponding boundary endpoints to obtain a closed diagram. Let $M_n$ be the matrix whose $(m,m')$ entry is the scalar Dubrovnik evaluation $P$ of this closure. Then $\det M_n$ is nonzero in $S$, its image is a non-zero-divisor in $T$, and the standard matching tangles are linearly independent over $T$. The assertion is over this universal coefficient extension and makes no independence claim after an arbitrary nonflat specialization.

Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

Fix $n\ge0$ and a rectangle with $n$ distinct ordered endpoints on its top edge and $n$ on its bottom edge. An ordinary $(n,n)$ tangle diagram is a finite generic planar projection in the rectangle of arcs joining these endpoints and finitely many closed curves, with an over/under marking at each transverse double point and no other singularities. Two diagrams are regularly isotopic when related by planar isotopy fixing the boundary and Reidemeister moves II and III. Their regular-isotopy classes form a monoid under vertical stacking, with the $n$ straight strands as its identity. In the fixed crossing chart, $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ by switching the marked crossing, $D_0$ is the through left/right smoothing, and $D_\infty$ is the cup-cap top/bottom smoothing. The displayed $D_+$ has its over-strand running southwest to northeast; with both strands directed downward it is the determinant-positive Artin crossing. A positive curl is a type-I kink with determinant crossing sign $+1$; a negative curl has sign $-1$. Define $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ to be the $T$-algebra obtained from the monoid algebra of these classes by imposing, in every interior disk, the Dubrovnik relations
$$D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty),\qquad \text{positive curl}=a\,\text{straight strand},\qquad \text{negative curl}=a^{-1}\,\text{straight strand},$$
and the free-circle relation that adjoining one disjoint circle with no crossings with the tangle multiplies it by $d$. The symbols $a,z_D,d$ are the images from the coefficient extension. No type-I move is imposed as a regular isotopy; its effect is represented by the displayed curl relations.

Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

By [F1], it returns `REJECT` exactly for the stated invalid cases, and an accepted string gives a finite signed braid word. Parsing a finite string terminates. For fixed $n$, there are finitely many matching connectors. By [F4], each connector has a standard descending class. For each matching, draw its finitely many open strands as simple polygonal arcs in $R$ with the fixed rational endpoints. Choose their interior vertices in general position and approximate them sufficiently closely by rational coordinates, preserving the endpoints and avoiding self-crossings, tangencies, and triple points. Assign each crossing so that the earlier strand is over the later one. This gives a rational generic descending code for the connector, so Step 3’s ordered search has a witness and terminates. Step 5 uses the explicit rational closure arcs $C_j$ in the algorithm. For $j<k$, $x_j<x_k$ and $\epsilon_j>\epsilon_k$, so their exterior lanes are nested and disjoint; they meet $R$ only at the prescribed endpoints. Thus each trace entry is a finite closed diagram without a closure-code search. The number of basis tangles and generator matrices is finite.

For each reducer input $D$, the Step 4 traversal is determined by the endpoint labels, retained segment labels, and current crossing or smoothing pairings. Thus the crossing count $r(D)$ and bad-crossing count $b(D)$ are well defined. At a terminal input, the algorithm reduces a crossingless tangle to its matching, simplifies a descending tangle leaf, or evaluates a descending closed diagram by its curls and free circles using [F2]. At a selected bad crossing, [F3] shows that switching keeps $r$ fixed and lowers $b$ by one, while either smoothing lowers $r$ by one. Every recursive child therefore has a smaller lexicographic pair.

Assume by strong induction that every reducer input with smaller pair terminates. Each recursive node has at most three children, and by [F3] every child has a smaller pair than its parent. Well-founded induction therefore gives a finite reduction tree for every generator-matrix column and every closed trace entry.

The recursive reductions apply the defining skein relation, and their terminal matching coordinates are unique by [F4]. Thus the finite matrix products give the coordinates of $\Phi_n(b_\beta)$ by [F5]. Pairing with the computed trace row yields $d^{-n}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})=\tau_n(b_\beta)$ by [F2]. By [F6], the algorithm's $w,c$ are the determinant writhe and component count of this oriented closure. Its prescribed final multiplication is therefore exactly $-(-1)^c a^{-w}d^{n-1}\tau_n(b_\beta)$. Only powers of the units $a,d$ are inverted, so no division by $z$ occurs.

current_manifest_record.statement:
Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data, and fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their gluing is the standard oriented three-sphere. Specialize the framed-link Kauffman bracket skein module of $H$ to the coefficient field and root fixed above. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H')$, define the handlebody pairing $B_\Sigma(x,y)$ by gluing the two framed skeins and evaluating the resulting closed marked three-manifold with the normalized root surgery invariant. Define

$$\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H')\}, \qquad V_p(\Sigma)=\mathcal K_A(H)/\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma).$$

This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.

**External normalization input.** In this Definition the closed marked evaluation is the BHMV TQFT normalization, not merely the raw signature-normalized closed invariant $\theta_p$ of the Kirby lemma. BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum §11 pp.23–25 give
$$Z_p(M,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}(\kappa^3)^w\theta_p(M),\qquad \Delta_\pm=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{\pm3}.$$
Thus $Z_p(S^3,0)=\eta$ and $Z_p(S^2\times S^1,0)=1$. These nonzero normalizations and the registered Wall-sign weight are part of the pairing. BHMV Proposition1.9, p.891, identifies EXACTLY this radical quotient computed with two complementary handlebodies with its universal state space. This external identification supplies well-definedness of the presented model; its finite basis and gluing are the separate following lemmas. The selected $\kappa$ remains a sixth root, with one weight step acting by its cube. The source itself is only used at these located statements/constructions, not as a claimed locally reconstructed universal-construction proof.

**Source hypotheses for this identification.** The normalized BHMV closed invariant is multiplicative and involutive, so BHMV Proposition 1.1 gives its cobordism-generated quantization functor at this fixed root; extend its coefficients to $\mathbb C$ as stated above. BHMV Theorem 1.7 supplies both hypotheses needed for Proposition 1.9: its Kauffman bracket relations let that proposition replace the free bordism module by the specialized skein module, and its surgery axioms give the surjectivity and radical-kernel description. The corresponding weighted Lagrangian version is the BHMV skein TQFT with integral weights and Lagrangians in place of $p_1$-structures, as described by Gilmer–Masbaum in §11; their one-weight square-root multiplier is matched to the selected BHMV sixth root by $\kappa_{\mathrm{GM}}=\kappa^3$. In that section Lemma 11.1 states the weighted surgery axiom and Remark 11.3 applies it to the handlebody skein presentation; the source refers the Lemma 11.1 proof to the BHMV argument rather than repeating it. These are imported source inputs, not a locally reconstructed proof, and they do not add another quotient or change the state-space interface.

Assume full AC for the surgery-presentation and universal-construction inputs below. Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, put $r=p/2$ and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and use the selected BHMV sixth root $\kappa$ satisfying $\kappa^6=A^{-6-(p+1)p/2}$. Fix a closed oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ with its Lagrangian and weighted anomaly data. Let $I_\Sigma$ be the finite union of its marked ribbon-end bands, with each band labeled by its specified simple object $a_j\in\{0,\ldots,r-2\}$. Fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their oriented gluing is the standard $S^3$; the boundary bands on $H$ and $H'$ are identified by the marking, with labels dualized on the oppositely oriented side.

For a banded boundary link $I$ in $\partial H$, let $\mathcal K_A(H;I)$ be the complex specialization of the relative Jones–Kauffman skein module generated by framed banded links in $H$ meeting $\partial H$ transversely in exactly $I$, modulo framed isotopy fixed on $\partial H$ and the following local relations in interior balls. In a chart where the over-strand runs southwest to northeast and the under-strand northwest to southeast, let $L_A$ join the two left endpoints and the two right endpoints, and let $L_B$ join the top endpoints and the bottom endpoints, with blackboard framing. Impose $[L_\times]=A[L_A]+A^{-1}[L_B]$. If $O$ is a zero-framed trivial circle bounding a disk disjoint from the rest of the link, impose $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. The empty link is allowed.

Let $\widetilde I_\Sigma$ be the boundary link obtained by replacing each band $I_j$ by $a_j$ parallel bands, deleting it when $a_j=0$. On $\mathcal K_A(H;\widetilde I_\Sigma)$, the identity-coefficient Jones–Wenzl projector $p_{a_j}$ acts on the corresponding parallel strands in a boundary collar. Define the colored relative skein module by $\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)=P_{\mathbf a}\mathcal K_A(H;\widetilde I_\Sigma)$, where $P_{\mathbf a}$ is the product of these mutually disjoint boundary projectors. Every denominator in these projectors is among $[2],\ldots,[a_j]$, which are nonzero because $a_j\le r-2$. When $I_\Sigma$ is empty, this is the ordinary closed-link module $\mathcal K_A(H)$.

For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$, glue their matching boundary bands and idempotents. This gives a closed colored ribbon graph $\Gamma$ in the standard $S^3$. Define the handlebody pairing by $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma,w)$, using the normalized root surgery evaluation and the weight $w$ prescribed by the fixed Lagrangian data. This is the BHMV sesquilinear pairing: it is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$ for the coefficient involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$. Define

$$\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)\}, \qquad V_p(\Sigma)=\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)/\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma).$$

This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.

**External normalization input.** In this Definition the closed marked evaluation is the BHMV TQFT normalization, not merely the raw signature-normalized closed invariant $\theta_p$ of the Kirby lemma. BHMV §2 pp.897–898 and Gilmer–Masbaum §11 pp.23–25 give
$$Z_p(M,\Gamma,w)=\eta^{b_0(M)+b_1(M)}(\kappa^3)^w\theta_p(M,\Gamma),\qquad \Delta_\pm=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{\pm3}.$$ 
Let $g_p=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{2p}(-1)^mA^{m^2}$, and let the bar denote the BHMV involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$. references.title: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Mustafa Hajij, and Kyle Istvan, Framed Knots, arXiv:1910.10257v6 (2020)

current_manifest_record.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $n\ge1$, and let $V$ be an $R$-valued invariant of unframed oriented knots of type at most $n$. Then $D_nV(K)=0$ whenever the degree-$n$ chord diagram of the $n$-singular knot $K$ has a chord that intersects no other chord. This is the 1T vanishing law for unframed symbols. In the framed category no universal 1T vanishing law holds: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, integer-valued framed self-linking has type at most $1$ and has derivative $2$ on a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

citations.quote:
Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. The same formula defines $D_mV$ for an invariant of framed knots on framed singular knots, counting both double points and framing zeroes among the $m$ singularities. For one double point it reads $V(K_+)-V(K_-)$; the zero resolutions use the local normal-section model just specified. An invariant has **type at most $n$** if $D_{n+1}V$ vanishes on every $(n+1)$-singular object in its category. It has **exact type $n$** if it has type at most $n$ but not type at most $n-1$. Type at most $-1$ means the zero invariant, so a nonzero type-at-most-zero invariant has exact type zero. For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot
$K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$, its normal bundle is
$\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, oriented so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a
positive basis of a normal fibre gives the ambient orientation. A **framing**
of $K$ is a homotopy class through smooth nowhere-zero sections of $\nu K$.
The normal bundle is made a smooth vector bundle under this axiom; a framed
knot includes the section class as data, not a choice made afterwards. For the
relative integer use the round metric transferred from the unit sphere in
$\mathbb R^4$ by the explicit diffeomorphism
$$x\longmapsto\left(\frac{2x}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2},\frac{\lVert x\rVert^2-1}{1+\lVert x\rVert^2}\right),\qquad\infty\longmapsto(0,0,0,1).$$
It induces a smooth bundle metric on $\nu K$. The resulting winding number is
independent of the metric: any two smooth fibre metrics interpolate through
positive metrics and the corresponding angle maps are homotopic.

Given a reference framing $[s_0]$ and another framing $[s_1]$, use a bundle
metric and the positive quarter-turn $J$ on each oriented normal plane. Choose
representatives $s_0,s_1$ and normalize both to unit sections
$\widehat s_i(x):=s_i(x)/\lVert s_i(x)\rVert$. Write
$$\widehat s_1(x)=\cos\theta(x)\widehat s_0(x)+\sin\theta(x)J\widehat s_0(x).$$
The resulting map $S^1\to S^1$ has a continuous angle lift along a parameter
interval $[0,1]$: subdivide into finitely many intervals whose images lie in
open semicircles and choose consecutive local arguments agreeing at endpoints.
Since the map is closed, the lift satisfies $\theta(1)-\theta(0)=2\pi m$ for
some $m\in\mathbb Z$; different lifts differ by a constant multiple of
$2\pi$, and homotopies keep $m$ fixed. Conversely, the difference between
$\theta(t)$ and $\theta(0)+2\pi mt$ is periodic, so linear interpolation of
these angles gives a homotopy to the degree-$m$ rotation of $\widehat s_0$.
Every integer occurs by such a rotation. Thus $m$ classifies the framing class
relative to $[s_0]$ and gives the **relative framing integer**. Once a reference
framing is supplied, the framing classes are an integer torsor; no absolute
integer is assigned before choosing a reference.

The **self-linking number** of a framed knot $(K,[s])$ is the linking number
of $K$ with a sufficiently small push-off along $s$, oriented parallel to $K$.
The push-off and its integer are independent of the representative section,
small radius, and normalized tubular chart by the preceding well-definedness
result.

If a compact oriented surface $\Sigma$ is supplied with boundary $K$, its
**Seifert framing relative to $\Sigma$** is the homotopy class of the inward
unit conormal to $K$ in $\Sigma$, viewed as a nonzero normal section to $K$ in
$S^3$. This definition is relative to the supplied surface; it neither asserts
that every knot bounds such a surface nor asserts the self-linking-zero result.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be an
oriented smooth embedded circle and let $s$ be a smooth nowhere-zero section of
its normal bundle. For any tubular neighbourhood chart that is the inclusion
on the zero section and identifies each vertical normal fibre with the ambient
normal quotient by the identity, the curve $K_{\varepsilon s}$ obtained by
mapping the graph of $\varepsilon s$ into $S^3$ is an embedded oriented circle
disjoint from $K$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. The integer
linking number of $K$ with $K_{\varepsilon s}$ is independent of the sufficiently
small radius, of the representative section in its homotopy class, and of the
normalized tubular chart. It therefore defines a self-linking integer of the
framing class $[s]$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram
of a knot $K$ with blackboard framing $b_D$. The self-linking number of the
framed knot $(K,b_D)$ equals the diagram writhe:
$$\operatorname{sl}(K,b_D)=\operatorname{wr}(D).$$
More generally, let $D$ be a regular oriented diagram of an oriented link
$L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$, and let $b_{D,i}$ be the blackboard framing
of $K_i$ induced by its component subdiagram. Then
$\operatorname{sl}(K_i,b_{D,i})=\operatorname{wr}_i(D)\qquad(1\le i\le r).$ Total writhe of a link still includes
the signs of mixed crossings, while the sum of component self-linking numbers
uses only self-crossings.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

The input is a finite regular oriented link diagram together with its declared
components. If it does not have exactly two components, return
`invalid-input`. For a two-component diagram $D$, initialize $s:=0$ and make
one pass over its finite crossing list. At each crossing whose branches lie on
different components, add
$$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$$
to $s$, where the determinant is taken in the oriented projection plane; ignore
self-crossings. Return $s/2$. The even-sum lemma establishes that this output is
an integer and is the diagram's linking number.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On every finite regular oriented diagram
with exactly two components, the crossing-scan algorithm halts after one
iteration per crossing and returns the integer half-sum of the mixed crossing
signs. On an input with any other number of components it returns
`invalid-input` after the finite component-count check.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $K$ be an $n$-singular knot with an isolated chord corresponding to the double point $p$. Its two preimages split the parameter circle into arcs $A$ and $B$. Isolation means no other marked double point has one preimage on each of $A$ and $B$. Choose a regular projection. There are finitely many ordinary crossings between the arcs. Switch them one at a time until every crossing has the $A$-branch over the $B$-branch. Each switch changes $D_nV$ by, up to sign, the $(n+1)$-fold difference on the knot with that ordinary crossing newly marked; this is zero by [F1]. Thus these switches preserve $D_nV(K)$.

For the framed branch, let $V$ be integer-valued self-linking. On a regular framed diagram compare a unit representative of its framing section $f$ with the unit blackboard normal section $b$. Their oriented fibrewise angle defines a map $S^1\to S^1$; let $\tau(f,b)\in\mathbb Z$ be its degree. In the tubular coordinates determined by $(b,Jb)$, the push-off along $f$ winds $\tau(f,b)$ times meridionally relative to the blackboard push-off. A positive meridian links the core once, since its oriented normal disk meets the core once with the sign fixed by the positive frame $(T,b,Jb)$. Thus $\operatorname{sl}(K,f)=\operatorname{sl}(K,b)+\tau(f,b)$; [F9] supplies the unit-twist normalization, and this local orientation calculation fixes its sign. Equivalently, each positive turn creates a local clasp with two positive mixed crossings, and [F7]–[F8] give the same linking increment. By [F6], $\operatorname{sl}(K,b)=\operatorname{wr}(D)$. For a framed singular knot with two disjoint singularities, all changes outside their local balls are fixed. Inside each ball, resolving a double point changes only that crossing's writhe contribution and local angle path; resolving a framing zero changes only the local angle path. Winding degrees add under concatenation, so the four self-linking values have the form $C+c_1\epsilon_1+c_2\epsilon_2$ for constants independent of $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$. Their alternating second difference is $(C+c_1+c_2)-(C+c_1-c_2)-(C-c_1+c_2)+(C-c_1-c_2)=0$. This covers any pair of double-point or framing-zero singularities, so self-linking has type at most $1$. On a one-chord diagram with blackboard framing, the two crossing resolutions have writhes $+1$ and $-1$ and zero relative twist; their derivative is $1-(-1)=2$ by [F3] and [F6]. This is nonzero over $\mathbb Z$, so no universal framed 1T vanishing law is valid. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption enters only through [F4]–[F9] and [A1].

The consistent over-under assignment lets the lifts of the interiors of $A$ and $B$ lie in opposite open half-spaces bounded by a plane through $p$. Cap each arc on its own side by a short boundary-parallel arc to obtain oriented singular knots $A^\circ$ and $B^\circ$ carrying the remaining marked double points. The two resolutions at $p$ are the connected sums $A^\circ\#B^\circ$ and $B^\circ\#A^\circ$. An orientation-preserving half-turn of the round $S^3$ that exchanges the two balls of the connected-sum decomposition carries the first knot, with its orientation, to the second; the path of rotations through angles from $0$ to $\pi$ is an ambient isotopy. Hence the two resolutions are ambient-isotopic, so their $V$-values agree and $D_nV(K)=0$.

native_decision.evidence: Read the complete replacement proof and CDM §8.5, printed pp.231–232. A Morse critical chart has nonzero horizontal tangent, so the short factor is O(ds/s); a long endpoint has separated denominator and smooth numerator O(ds). The highest surviving short chord must have a higher long endpoint, otherwise consecutive endpoints kill it by 1T. Integrating that endpoint first supplies delta_k, and the displayed nested logarithmic integral is S, including arbitrary k. Independent critical charts handle the corner intersections; m=0 contributes no needle endpoint. Unlike the removed branch cancellation, this estimates actual individual pairing terms without identifying distinct diagrams. The needle uniformity explicitly depends on a compact smooth family with uniformly nondegenerate charts and separation; it cannot license arbitrary degenerating families. The drawing is a schematic of the short/long cases. Reader convergence repair accepted at those literal hypotheses.

citations.quote:
Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions. Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.82,thick]
  \draw (2,0) -- (2,3);
  \draw[very thick] (1,0) -- (0.5,1.5) -- (0,3);
  \draw (0,0) -- (0.48,1.44);
  \draw (0.52,1.56) -- (1,3);
  \node at (1,-0.32) {$((1\ 2)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1,3.32) {$((2\ 1)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1.2,2.55) {$\sigma_1$};
  \node at (2.45,1.5) {$t$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

derivations.claim: Near a nondegenerate maximum, use the Morse coordinate $s=\sqrt{t_c-t}$ from [F2]. The two local branch functions satisfy $z_+(s)=z_c+a s+O(s^2)$ and $z_-(s)=z_c-a s+O(s^2)$ for some $a\ne0$; this follows because the tangle or knot immersion has nonzero tangent and $dt/ds=0$ at the critical point, so its tangent there is horizontal. Hence $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$ and the short logarithmic form has absolute size at most $C\,ds/s$. A minimum has the same estimate after reversing $t$.

For a long chord with one endpoint on the needle and one outside it, compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for $|z-z'|$ on each compact branch chart. In the Morse parameter $s$, both endpoint evaluations are smooth, so the one-form $d\log(z-z')$ has norm at most $C\,ds$. The range of $s$ along a width-$\varepsilon$ needle is at most $C\varepsilon$, since $|z_+(s)-z_-(s)|\asymp s$. Thus integrating such a chord endpoint over any subinterval of the needle costs at most $C\varepsilon$. This is a direct absolute estimate for each pairing term and does not identify diagrams obtained from opposite branch choices. The constants are uniform in the stated compact smooth family.

Order the chord endpoints on the small oriented component arc through a maximum. Consider the short chord closest to $t_c$. If no other endpoint lies on the arc between its two ends through the critical point, it is isolated under the tangle or circle 1T rule and its diagram vanishes by [F1, F3]. Thus every nonzero pairing with short chords has an endpoint of a long chord on this arc above the short chord closest to the critical point. The same argument, with height reversed, applies at a minimum.

Suppose a nonzero pairing contains $k\ge1$ short chords at one critical point. Write their Morse parameters as $0<\delta_k<\cdots<\delta_1<S$, where $\delta_k$ is closest to the critical point and $S\le C\varepsilon$. By step 2.1, an endpoint of a long chord lies on the small arc above the chord at $\delta_k$, so its parameter $s$ satisfies $0<s<\delta_k$. Integrating this long endpoint first contributes at most $C\delta_k$ by step 1.2, while each short factor is bounded by $C\,d\delta_j/\delta_j$ by step 1.1. The resulting local absolute integral is bounded by $C\int_0^S\frac{d\delta_1}{\delta_1}\int_0^{\delta_1}\frac{d\delta_2}{\delta_2}\cdots\int_0^{\delta_{k-1}}\frac{d\delta_k}{\delta_k}\,\delta_k=CS$, using $\int_0^a(d\delta/\delta)\delta=a$. If no short chord occurs, every factor is smooth on the compactified branch chart. Away from critical levels all within-chord denominators are bounded away from zero; at a corner involving several distinct critical points, apply this same estimate independently in each critical chart. current_manifest_record.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

derivations.claim: The monic relations make $\mathbb A$ free over $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb R$ free over $\mathbb Z[h]$, each with basis $1,X$. Both relations are homogeneous for the displayed degrees. For the odd maps, the merge quotient is well-defined because $p(C_1-C_2)=0$. The split formula is independent of whether $j(C)=C_1$ or $C_2$, since $(C_1-C_2)\wedge C_1=(C_1-C_2)\wedge C_2=C_1\wedge C_2$.

In $\mathbb R$, associativity, commutativity and the unit law follow from quotient-ring multiplication. On the basis $1,X$, the counit composites $(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\epsilon)\Delta$ both send $1\mapsto1$ and $X\mapsto X$. Cocommutativity follows from the symmetric formulas for $\Delta(1)$ and $\Delta(X)$. For coassociativity, both iterated comultiplications send $X$ to $X\otimes X\otimes X$ and send $1$ to $1\otimes X\otimes X+X\otimes1\otimes X+X\otimes X\otimes1-h(1\otimes1\otimes X+1\otimes X\otimes1+X\otimes1\otimes1)+h^2 1\otimes1\otimes1.$ Thus the unit, counit and coassociativity axioms hold.

On the ordered basis $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$, each of $\Delta m$, $(m\otimes\mathrm{id})(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)$, and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes m)(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})$ has respective outputs $1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h1\otimes1,\quad X\otimes X,\quad X\otimes X,\quad hX\otimes X.$ Therefore the Frobenius identities hold. On every cube square, the two unsigned composites agree by tensor functoriality on disjoint circles, associativity for two merges, coassociativity for two splits, or the checked Frobenius identities for a merge-split pair. Opposite cube signs make the two signed composites cancel, so the Bar–Natan differential squares to zero. A based odd cube with the square-compatible sign data in [A1] is also a cochain complex: the coefficient of each height-two state in $d^2$ is the sum of its two signed composites, zero by the defining condition. The right marked action commutes with merges because the quotient carries $Z_p$ to the marked output circle. It commutes with splits because $((C_1-C_2)\wedge j(z))\wedge Z_p=(C_1-C_2)\wedge j(z\wedge Z_p)$, including a split of the marked circle: either lift of the marked output differs by $C_1-C_2$, whose extra wedge vanishes. Also $X^2$ acts by zero. Every state module is free over $\mathbb A$: choose the exterior products of unmarked circle generators as module basis and append $Z_p$ on the right for their $X$ multiples. Modulo $2$ this action is precisely the even marked action, and reduction of $\mathbb R$ modulo $(2,h)$ retains that action through $\mathbb B$, rather than setting $X=0$. Existence of such odd sign assignments, the mod-2 comparison as a homotopy equivalence, and the localized rank-one condition are not claimed by this Definition; they are separate assertions of the foundations lemma. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

For the empty link diagram, use its single empty resolution state and empty tensor term $\mathbb Q$ in cohomological and quantum degree $0$, with zero differential. Its induced decreasing filtration is $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pC_L(\varnothing;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $p>0$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot admitting a finite regular diagram $D$ with $n$ positive crossings and no negative crossings, and let $k$ be the number of circles in its oriented resolution. Then Rasmussen’s invariant satisfies
$$
s(K)=n-k+1.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $K^\dagger$ be the reverse mirror of an oriented knot $K$. Then
$$
s(K^\dagger)=-s(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with Hedden–Ording twist parameter $t=2$. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with Hedden–Ording twist parameter $t=2$. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

current_manifest_record.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with Hedden–Ording twist parameter $t=2$. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
