citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim: Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. These conditions verify the individual isotopies and the displayed endpoint. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and Hedden–Ording $t=2$ framing retained. The complete integer arrows and finite move list are recorded with the computation data below; neither a knot-table name nor a Floer rank identifies this knot.

The orientation junction preserves the normalized filtered invariant without an ambient invertibility assumption. For a doubly-pointed diagram of an oriented knot $J$, swapping only $w,z$ presents $J^r$. The actual disks are unchanged and their two marked degrees exchange, so $I:[x,i,j]\mapsto[x,j,i]$ is a Laurent-linear swap-filtered chain isomorphism to that diagram. The carried zero-Seifert cap gives $A'(x)=-A(x)$. The relative disk index then gives $M'(x)=M(x)-2A(x)+c$ for one integer $c$, so $I$ has constant full Maslov degree $c$. Compose it with the normalized same-oriented-knot conjugation of [F4], whose Maslov degree is zero and which swaps the two filtrations, including its inverse and homotopies. The composite is an ordinary bifiltered equivalence to $J^r$ of degree $c$. Its vertical hat quotient is an isomorphism between the two total three-sphere hat groups, each concentrated in normalized Maslov degree zero; hence $c=0$. This proves equality of the normalized inclusion thresholds for $J,J^r$. It also identifies their normalized bigraded knot Floer homologies. Apply this to the grid in step 1.1. Reflecting its columns, $O_r\mapsto11-O_r$ and $X_r\mapsto11-X_r$, gives a grid for its mirror: $(x,y,h)\mapsto(-x,y,h)$ reverses ambient orientation and keeps vertical strands over horizontal strands. No further knot-recognition premise is needed for this second grid.

Compute the multi-pointed hat filtered grid differential of each explicit grid: set every $O$-variable of the full minus grid complex to zero and retain every $O$-empty rectangle, including those containing $X$-markings. For a permutation state $p$, use $M_O(p)=I(p,p)-I(p,O)-I(O,p)+I(O,O)+1$ and $2A(p)=M_O(p)-M_X(p)-11$, with marks at half-integer cell centers and $I$ counting pairs strictly increasing in both coordinates. In the quotient $Q=C/F_0C$ retain exactly the states with $A>0$. Only Maslov degrees $-1,0,1$ enter $H_0(Q)$; discarding the outgoing differential from degree $-1$ does not change that group. The inventory is exhaustive by the following finite assignment recurrence. For used columns $S$ in the first $r=|S|$ rows, choosing $c\notin S$ increments the state-state term by $|\{b\in S:b<c\}|$. Add $-\#\{k\ge r:O_k\ge c\}-\#\{k<r:O_k<c\}$ to obtain the Maslov increment; the Alexander increment is the corresponding $X$ expression minus its $O$ expression. Accumulating the resulting two-variable polynomial over the $4096$ column subsets counts every permutation exactly once. For every retained state and ordered pair of distinct rows, take the corresponding oriented torus rectangle; the ordered pair includes both cyclic orientations, so complementary rectangles are counted in their respective directions. Reject a rectangle containing an interior state point or an $O$-marking, and retain every other rectangle, including those containing $X$-markings. Its output transposes the two chosen columns; discard that output only when its Alexander value is at most zero. Summing modulo two gives the actual quotient matrix. The first grid has $45\,824$ retained states, $159\,685$ rectangle orbits, including $24\,181$ with positive $X$ multiplicity, and $158\,523$ nonzero matrix entries. The reflected grid has $6080$ retained states and $11\,474$ rectangle orbits and nonzero entries. Every term has Maslov drop one and Alexander drop exactly its $X$ multiplicity; actual matrix multiplication gives $d^2=0$ in both quotients. These are the literal rectangle counts of [L1], rather than a formal-domain enumeration.

Exact column elimination over $\mathbb F_2$ gives $$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}&\dim Q_1&\dim Q_0&\dim Q_{-1}&\operatorname{rank}d_1&\operatorname{rank}d_0\\\hline G&12347&17919&15558&8384&9535\\G^{\mathrm{mirror}}&4385&1463&232&1243&220.\end{array}$$ To specify the finite rank operation, encode a column by its row bits; repeatedly cancel its highest nonzero row with the previously retained pivot column at that row, or retain it as a new pivot if no such column exists. The counts of retained pivots are the displayed ranks. The saved complete columns and pivot-reduction traces give these computations directly. A separate exact verification used the complete joint assignment polynomial, checked every state and both normalized grid gradings, reconstructed every retained rectangle, checked $d^2$, and recomputed both ranks. Thus $$\dim H_0(Q_G)=17919-8384-9535=0,\qquad\dim H_0(Q_{G^{\mathrm{mirror}}})=1463-1243-220=0.$$ This uses the full filtered quotients, including the positive-$X$ terms in the first matrix.

Apply [L1]'s absolutely normalized filtered comparison and specialize all marking variables to zero. The multi-pointed hat filtered grid complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the doubly-pointed full hat complex tensored with $V^{\otimes11}$, where the two degrees of $V$ are $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$. Its total Maslov-zero homology is consequently one-dimensional, represented by the normalized three-sphere generator tensored with the sole degree-zero vector of $V^{\otimes11}$. Its filtration threshold is exactly $\tau(J)$: inclusion into that tensor factor and projection onto it are filtered degree-zero chain maps, so they give both threshold inequalities. The exact sequence $0\to F_0C\to C\to Q\to0$ and step 4.1 show that this total Maslov-zero class comes from $H_0(F_0C)$ for each grid. Hence $\tau(J)\le0$ and $\tau(mJ)\le0$, for the actual knot $J$ of step 1.1 and its mirror.

For completeness derive the required threshold sign from [F4]'s normalized reverse-mirror duality. Let $D$ be the finite normalized doubly-pointed full hat complex and write $t$ for its inclusion threshold. Its dual filtration is $F_sD^\vee=\{\lambda:\lambda(F_{-s-1}D)=0\}$. Choose a total generator cycle $z\in F_tD_0$. Then $z\notin\operatorname{im}(d:D_1\to D_0)+F_{t-1}D_0$: any such expression would give a homologous cycle at level $t-1$. Finite-dimensional linear algebra therefore gives a functional $\lambda$ vanishing on that sum and taking value one on $z$. It is a nonzero dual homology class at filtration $-t$. Conversely every functional at level $s<-t$ vanishes on $F_tD$, hence on $z$, and cannot represent the nonzero dual class. Thus the dual threshold is exactly $-t$. The absolute normalization and full duality in [F4], together with the orientation junction of step 2.1, give $\tau(mJ)=-\tau(J)$. Combining the two actual quotient inequalities of step 5.1 forces $\tau(J)=0$. By step 2.1 this is the normalized tau value of the actual positive Whitehead double with Hedden–Ording parameter $t=2$ in the Statement.

The admitted diagram and framing in step 1.1 are also those of [F3]. That accepted finite Lee computation gives $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$. Together with the independently established normalized value in step 6.1 this proves both numerical assertions of the Statement. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: Peter S. Ozsvath, Andras I. Stipsicz, and Zoltan Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, Appendix B.4

current_manifest_record.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $G_0,G_1$ be finite planar grid diagrams, with vertical segments over horizontal segments and orientation from $O$ to $X$ in rows and $X$ to $O$ in columns, representing the same oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. A cyclic permutation moves the first row or column to the last position. A row commutation exchanges adjacent rows when the closed intervals between their respective $O$- and $X$-mark abscissae are disjoint or one lies in the interior of the other; a column commutation is defined by the same condition on the intervals between marking heights. A stabilization chooses a marked cell and temporarily removes its marking together with the other markings in its row and column. It splits that row and column into two, places the three removed markings, and adds one new $O$-mark and one new $X$-mark so that every row and column again has one of each. In the four-cell subdivision of the chosen cell, exactly three cells are marked: the chosen marking type appears twice, the other type once, and any one corner may be the empty cell; the two other markings removed from the original row and column are placed outside this block in the new row and column. A destabilization is the inverse operation. Then a finite sequence of cyclic permutations, commutations, stabilizations, and destabilizations carries $G_0$ to $G_1$.

citations.quote: Let $G$ be a finite nonempty planar marked grid with vertical-over crossing convention. A horizontal segment is a cap if its two incident vertical segments both extend above it or both extend below it; otherwise it is monotone. A marked stabilization splits a marked cell into a two-by-two block with the chosen marking type twice at opposite corners, the other type once and one empty corner, preserving one of each type per row and column. A legal column commutation exchanges adjacent columns with disjoint or strictly nested closed vertical marking intervals. There is a finite sequence of marked stabilizations and legal commutations carrying $G$ to a grid in which every cap has no crossing and every monotone horizontal segment has exactly one crossing. Thus the resulting grid is bridge-like: slightly tilt its crossing-containing horizontal segments in the direction of height travel and round its empty caps to obtain a bridge diagram. Every operation respects the oriented $O,X$ convention of the grid-diagram definition, and the number of link components is unchanged. The decorated planar diagram before and after the entire refinement is planar isotopic after rounding corners; in particular no Reidemeister move is needed for this refinement. No global grid-move generation theorem is assumed.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.
Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be
obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.

Assume countable choice. Let $D_0,D_1$ be nonempty oriented bridge diagrams that are planar isotopic with crossing decorations transported by the isotopy. Then any bridge-like grid rectification of $D_0$ is connected to any bridge-like grid rectification of $D_1$ by finitely many marked grid stabilizations, legal commutations and destabilizations. Here vertical strands pass over horizontal strands, a legal commutation exchanges adjacent rows or columns with disjoint or strictly nested closed marking intervals, and a stabilization is a three-mark two-by-two split preserving one $O$ and one $X$ per row and column. In particular the grid-move class assigned by bridge rectification depends only on the oriented decorated planar-isotopy class whenever that class is represented by bridge diagrams. No Reidemeister-move or global grid-isotopy generation theorem is used.

Assume countable choice. Suppose two nonempty oriented decorated planar diagrams differ by one Reidemeister move inside a disk, retaining the entire exterior and its boundary incidence. Each endpoint admits a bridge representative in its decorated planar-isotopy class. Let $D_0^\prime,D_1^\prime$ be any bridge diagrams planar isotopic to the respective endpoints. Then any bridge-like grid rectifications of $D_0^\prime,D_1^\prime$ are connected by finitely many marked grid stabilizations, legal commutations and destabilizations. All signs, strand orientations and consistent strict over/under orders of R3 are included. The exterior diagram is arbitrary. A legal commutation exchanges adjacent rows or columns whose closed marking intervals are disjoint or strictly nested; a stabilization is a three-mark two-by-two split preserving one mark of each type in each row and column. No shared-endpoint switch is assumed as a primitive move. The conclusion uses no global grid-isotopy generation theorem.

derivations.claim: A knot grid is nonempty. Apply [F1] to each $G_i$, obtaining a finite grid-move sequence to a bridge-like grid $B_i$. Smooth $B_i$ as in that supplier to a bridge diagram $D_i$. Its crossing decorations and strand orientation agree with the original grid diagram, and the supplier proves planar isotopy after smoothing. Thus $D_0,D_1$ represent the same oriented knot. The three-mark splits and strict interval commutations in [F1] are among those specified here: the retained exterior row and column partners provide the two markings outside the stabilization block in the Statement. No unlisted shared-endpoint switch has been used.

By [F2] choose a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves from $D_0$ to $D_1$. Compose successive planar isotopies, and regard each remaining Reidemeister move as an edge between its two decorated planar-isotopy classes. The sequence now traverses finitely many such classes, with the first and last represented by $D_0,D_1$. If there is no Reidemeister edge, these two diagrams are planar isotopic. Otherwise every intermediate representative is a regular diagram and has a bridge representative in its decorated planar-isotopy class by [F5]; choose the perturbation small enough that its crossings and decorations persist. Choose one bridge representative for each occurrence of a class in this finite sequence, keeping $D_0,D_1$ at its ends, and choose a bridge rectification there. The choices are finite; no stronger choice principle is invoked.

Across a Reidemeister edge, the chosen bridge representatives need only be planar isotopic to that edge's original endpoint diagrams. This is exactly the relative-representative interface of [F4], so their chosen grid rectifications are joined by actual grid moves, with every exterior strand included. Across an interval with only planar isotopy, [F3] joins the chosen rectifications. This also treats the sequence with no Reidemeister edge. The endpoint rectifications may be taken to be precisely $B_0,B_1$, because both suppliers apply to arbitrary rectifications. Concatenating the finitely many constituent finite sequences gives a sequence of allowed commutations, stabilizations and destabilizations from $B_0$ to $B_1$.

Prepend the refinement from $G_0$ to $B_0$ and append the reversed refinement from $B_1$ to $G_1$. Reversing a stabilization gives a destabilization and reversing a legal commutation gives a legal commutation, so all operations remain allowed. This produces the required finite sequence from $G_0$ to $G_1$. The proof needs no cyclic permutation, but allowing those additional moves in the Statement does not change the conclusion. The local suppliers cover all marking types and strand orientations, so the sequence preserves the prescribed oriented-knot convention throughout.

current_manifest_record.statement:
Let an object be a finite disjoint union of smooth embedded circles in the oriented plane $\mathbb R^2$, including the empty union. A cobordism from $C_0$ to $C_1$ is a compact smooth orientable surface properly embedded in $\mathbb R^2\times[0,1]$, with boundary $C_0\times\{0\}\sqcup C_1\times\{1\}$, product collars at those boundaries, and no other boundary. Surfaces are identified up to ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars. Compose cobordisms by gluing along their common boundary circles; the identity of $C$ is $C\times[0,1]$, and disjoint union gives the monoidal product.

Take the free abelian group on these isotopy classes as each morphism group, and extend composition bilinearly. Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the resulting preadditive monoidal category before local relations are imposed. Quotient its morphism groups by the following local relations, which are required to hold inside every surrounding cobordism. A sphere component is zero (the S relation). Adding a disjoint torus component multiplies a cobordism by $2$ (the T relation). For four disjoint disk patches numbered $1,2,3,4$, write $S_{ij}$ for the surface obtained by deleting the interiors of patches $i,j$ and joining their boundary circles by an orientable tube; the four-tube relation is $S_{12}+S_{34}=S_{13}+S_{24}$. The resulting preadditive monoidal quotient category is denoted $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$.

Work in the smooth category inherited from the oriented-link convention. In particular, an embedded bridge witness disk means the image of a smooth rank-two embedding of a planar disk, with ordinary smooth boundary or smooth transverse corners at its two marked endpoints; smoothness at a boundary or corner means local smooth extension in its charts. Witness parametrizations can be chosen for the finite disk families. This category convention does not require the knot arcs to meet the Heegaard surface transversely: tangential smooth crossings remain permitted.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $h$, let $k\ge1$, and put $m=h+k-1$. A **handlebody** is a compact three-manifold that is a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph. A **$2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for $S^3$** consists of a splitting $S^3=U_{\alpha}\cup_{\Sigma}U_{\beta}$ into handlebodies, two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$ of pairwise disjoint simple closed curves on $\Sigma$ that bound pairwise disjoint properly embedded disks in $U_{\alpha}$ and $U_{\beta}$, respectively, cutting each handlebody into exactly $k$ three-balls, and two ordered sets of distinct points $\mathbf w=(w_1,\ldots,w_k)$ and $\mathbf z=(z_1,\ldots,z_k)$ disjoint from the curves. Curves from different systems intersect transversely in finitely many points. Each component of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$ contains exactly one $w$-point and exactly one $z$-point. The diagram also includes trivial arc systems in the two handlebodies: the $\alpha$-arcs join $w_i$ to $z_i$, and the $\beta$-arcs join $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$, with indices modulo $k$. Each system is disjoint from its compression disks and is simultaneously boundary parallel: its arcs cobound pairwise disjoint embedded disks with arcs in the corresponding components of the attaching-system complement on $\Sigma$. Thus each ball obtained by compression contains one unknotted arc. Together the arcs form an oriented knot, oriented from $w_i$ to $z_i$ in $U_{\alpha}$ and from $z_i$ to $w_{i-1}$ in $U_{\beta}$. The diagram is **compatible with $K$** when this knot is orientation-preservingly ambient isotopic to $K$. For a grid diagram, compatibility uses the row and column orientation fixed in the grid definition, with $w$-points at $O$ and $z$-points at $X$. For a grid representing one knot, the basepoint pairs can be numbered cyclically in reverse order of travel along the oriented knot so that $w_i,z_i$ lie in the same component $A_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\alpha$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}$ lie in the same component $B_i$ of $\Sigma\setminus\boldsymbol\beta$.

Comparisons of these embedded diagrams allow **orientation-preserving diagram isomorphisms**: an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $S^3$ carrying the two handlebodies, their oriented Heegaard surface, the two attaching systems, the ordered $w,z$ points, and the two simultaneously boundary-parallel arc systems to the corresponding data. Equivalently one may specify the surface isomorphism together with its compatible collared extensions over both handlebodies carrying those arcs. The attaching systems are carried as systems; reordering their curve factors induces the corresponding product identification. Comparisons also allow **arc normalizations in the fixed splitting**: a smooth isotopy of the represented oriented knot, supported near the ordered marks and fixing each mark, during which every open connecting arc stays in its original handlebody and the two simultaneous boundary-parallel witness systems are retained or replaced by embedded witnesses for those same arcs. The surface, attaching curves, marked points and compression disks stay fixed. Such a normalization may replace a tangential marked crossing by a transverse one; the original data are not required to have neat arcs. This is a change of knot representative relative to the fixed surface, not a diagram isomorphism carrying both objects. Analytic and assigned grading data depending on the fixed surface diagram can be kept identical; the corresponding generator and disk-count identification is then the identity. Existence of normalizations with the required witnesses is a separate geometric assertion, not part of this definition. Such a comparison transports the represented oriented knot and any specified Seifert surface as well. For analytic data, it transports $j$, the surface area form, all chosen divisor neighborhoods and $J_t$ by the induced symmetric-product diffeomorphism. The comparison maps on generators and disk classes are their pushforwards under this map; compatibility with the count differential is a mathematical property to be proved. No identity action is part of this convention, even when the ambient diffeomorphism is isotopic to the identity.

The $m$-fold symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)=\Sigma^m/S_m$ is the space of unordered $m$-tuples of points of $\Sigma$, where $S_m$ permutes coordinates. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ be the quotient map. The product tori are the images $\mathbb T_{\alpha}=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_m)$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_m)$. Their intersection points are the generators. A **Whitney disk class** $\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps from a disk to $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ whose two boundary arcs lie on $\mathbb T_{\alpha}$ and $\mathbb T_{\beta}$ and whose endpoints are $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions with coefficients equal to local multiplicities. Write $n_{w_i}(\phi)$ and $n_{z_i}(\phi)$ for its local multiplicities at the marked points. An almost complex structure $J$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle with $J^2=-1$. Fix a complex structure $j$ and an area form on $\Sigma$. For $m>0$, choose a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ of nearly symmetric almost complex structures, constant near $t=0,1$: each $J_t$ agrees with the induced integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(j)$ on a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and of every divisor $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ for a chosen interior point $p$ of every complementary region, including every marked point, and tames the form descended from the product area form off that neighborhood. The path is a sufficiently small perturbation in this class. For $m=0$ the symmetric product is a point. Local multiplicities are intersection numbers with these divisors; positivity is a mathematical property to be proved, not an additional choice of disk counts. A $\mathbb J$-holomorphic strip representative is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(\Sigma)$ satisfying $\partial_{\tau}u+J_t(u)\partial_tu=0$, with $u(\tau,0)\in\mathbb T_{\alpha}$, $u(\tau,1)\in\mathbb T_{\beta}$, and limits $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$ as $\tau\to-\infty,+\infty$. Translation in $\tau$ defines an $\mathbb R$-action. The Maslov index $\mu(\phi)$ is the Fredholm index of the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at a representative of $\phi$; the relative Maslov grading convention is $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y)=\mu(\phi)-2\sum_{i=1}^{k}n_{w_i}(\phi)$, up to one overall additive constant.

A **periodic domain** is an integral two-chain in the complementary regions whose boundary is an integral sum of full $\alpha$- and $\beta$-curves; its local multiplicity at a marked point is the coefficient of the containing region. The pointed diagram is **admissible** when every nonzero periodic domain with $n_{w_i}=0$ for all $i$ has at least one positive and at least one negative region coefficient. A path $\mathbb J$ is **regular for a set of disk classes** when the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator at every holomorphic-strip representative in those classes is surjective. For a path regular on the classes used, let $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)$ be the space of strip representatives. If, for each generator $\mathbf x$, only finitely many pairs $(\mathbf y,\phi)$ with $\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing$, $\mu(\phi)=1$, and $n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0$ for every $i$ occur, and each quotient is finite, the multipointed full filtered minus module is the free module over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$ generated by $\mathbb T_{\alpha}\cap\mathbb T_{\beta}$, with differential
$$\partial^-\mathbf x=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\mathbf y),\;\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)\ne\varnothing\\\mu(\phi)=1,\; n_{w_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \forall i}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathbb J}(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)\,U_1^{n_{w_1}(\phi)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(\phi)}\mathbf y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is the count modulo two of the zero-dimensional quotient when it is finite. Quotienting by all $U_i$ leaves the fully blocked multipointed chain complex (the hat chain complex when $k=1$), with terms only from classes satisfying $n_{w_i}=0$ for every $i$; its Alexander-filtered associated-graded complex further retains only classes with every $n_{z_i}=0$. The relative Alexander grading convention is $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)$, with an overall additive constant. Each $U_i$ lowers Maslov grading by two and Alexander filtration by one. In a grid diagram, $\Sigma=T^2$, $h=1$, $k=n$, and $m=n$; the horizontal circles are the $\alpha$-curves, the vertical circles are the $\beta$-curves, and the $w$-points and $z$-points are the $O$- and $X$-markings respectively.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

current_manifest_record.statement:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For positive-rank triangle pieces choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Supply finite balanced polygon Morse data of rank $m=h+k-1\ge1$, with common $w,z$ marks, and no triple intersection of the product tori. Fix a Spin-c structure on the polygon cobordism and use the STRICT all-$w$ normalized strong admissibility condition of the named geometric lattice theorem. Use the same condition for its relevant boundary-pair sectors. The boundary systems have their actual complete $k$-ball cuts, and nearly symmetric geometry has exact constant product-angle generator charts. No $S^3$ or torsion restriction on the intermediate three-manifolds is made.

In the smooth topology, the genuine constant-collar end paths having no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and regularity for every actual index-one strip in the relevant sectors form an open dense subset of the allowed protected end paths. With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Their count-dimension-zero total sets are finite, and their count-dimension-one spaces compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. All nonnegative $w,z$ degrees are retained. These conclusions hold for the fixed total Spin-c label, across all its literal realized classes; they also hold for fixed degree vectors or fixed actual classes. The boundary consists exactly of the label-compatible rigid polygon–polygon faces and strip–polygon breakings, with additive marked vectors and actual exhaustive gluing collars. No sphere or one-torus disk bubble occurs in these polygon dimensions. This includes $k=1$.

For triangles the fixed count index is $\mu$, so rigid counts have $\mu=0$ and the chain-map boundary has $\mu=1$. In a generic one-parameter triangle family with fixed regular end data the universal count index is $\mu+1$: the index-minus-one universal counts are finite, and universal index-zero spaces have the parameter endpoints and strip–triangle boundaries. Thus the finite actual counts satisfy the weighted triangle chain-map equation and its auxiliary-data chain homotopy over $\mathbb F_2$. They may be specialized to the two-color ring by sending every $w$ variable to $U$ and every $z$ variable to $V$. No top-generator cycle, handle-map inverse, arbitrary diagram invariance or absolute grading is part of this assertion.

Assume countable choice. Let $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$ be a strictly strongly admissible pointed Heegaard triple for a decorated knot cobordism, with the strong condition normalized at ALL $w$ marks. Fix one Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ and nonnegative $w,z$-multiplicities. In positive symmetric rank $m=h+k-1>0$, among the auxiliary Heegaard data first choose an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no common intersection of three attaching families, following the pair generators and transporting the actual Spin-c label and strict admissibility. Such positive-rank representatives exist. Fix that representative; this is an explicit curve choice, not a claim that varying the almost-complex tensor alone regularizes constant triangles on the original arbitrary fixed triple.

At rank $m=0$, keep the original empty attaching systems: the target is one point and no triple-torus exclusion is imposed. Its unique constant triangle, when its assigned Spin-c label and zero marked-degree vectors match the specified ones, is regular of index zero and contributes one; all other specified-label or positive-degree sets are empty. The fixed index-one and universal index-minus-one spaces are empty, and a matching one-parameter family is the parameter interval.

In positive rank choose regular end data in the open dense set of allowed genuine constant-collar paths described in the proof. For generic fixed source-dependent almost-complex data compatible with those ends, the Maslov-index-zero triangle moduli spaces used in the triangle-count map are regular zero-manifolds and finite. For generic one-parameter families with those fixed regular ends, the universal triangle moduli spaces are regular with the parameter included in the expected dimension; slice counts are taken at regular parameter values. The compactified one-dimensional Maslov-index-one triangle spaces have precisely the broken triangle/strip strata, with actual gluing collars. In these dimensions no nonconstant one-torus boundary degeneration is allowed: its index contribution is at least two and the remaining triangle would have negative count dimension. In a one-parameter family the compactified universal index-zero spaces additionally have the two parameter-endpoint strata; the zero-dimensional universal index-minus-one spaces define the homotopy terms.

The mod-two boundary counts give the weighted bilinear triangle chain-map equation and its chain homotopy. Inserting an actual intermediate cycle gives the corresponding one-input chain-map equation. All nonnegative marked multiplicities and the fixed Spin-c extension are retained, including intermediate closed three-manifolds beyond $S^3$ and multiple mark pairs. No additional ends arise from sphere bubbling, escape through nonzero periodic domains or uncontrolled marked-point multiplicities. This analytic assertion does not itself establish that a named top generator is a cycle or prove invariance under changing the chosen attaching curves.

derivations.claim: **Choice scope.** Fix the actual compact smooth cobordism, decoration, Spin-c structure and, for a comparison, the two actual decompositions. A compact smooth input has finite atlas/handle data. A Morse decomposition has finitely many critical points; a generic Cerf comparison has finitely many exceptional times (Zemke Lemma 11.18, p.80, and Theorem 11.5, pp.74 and 84–85). Choosing a finite list of charts, gradient-like fields, band neighborhoods, puncturing balls and standard auxiliary classes uses finite choice only. No choice of one decomposition for every cobordism is required: existence and pairwise comparison are quantified separately for arbitrary given inputs.

The dividing surface and boundary data meet the source category in [F1]: basepoints alternate, the dividing set separates the two regions, every three-manifold component meets the link, and every four-manifold component meets the divided surface. Closed dividing curves are allowed by its properly embedded one-manifold definition. The two-color assignment in [F3] is compatible on every elementary piece, including multicomponent and multiply based intermediate links. Its curvature is zero, so the imported curved maps are genuine maps of complexes over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$.

Use the elementary maps of [F1] for the chosen parametrized Kirby decomposition, with [F2]'s actual auxiliary cycles and the fixed restricted Spin-c labels. Their finite polynomial counts, chain-map property and compatibility with the natural Heegaard transition maps are supplied by that external construction. Thus their composition is the displayed representative. If a component has an empty incoming or outgoing end, apply [F1]'s standard puncturing prescription before composing, not an undefined intermediate empty-link Heegaard diagram. No graph-TQFT reduction or hat-only construction is substituted for this two-variable map.

For that finite list of diagrams, the homotopy and periodic-domain data are countably indexed: use the finite-cell models of the compact manifolds and finite products of circles, and integer words in their finite attaching data; Spin-c extensions form a subset of a finitely generated integral cohomology torsor. Integer degrees, multiplicities, polygon types and neck lengths in $\mathbb N$ are countable indices as well. The count theorem [F4] supplies coherent perturbations relative to faces and fixed ends, rather than making independent choices at every real parameter value. Model counts and the finite move identities of [F1] use such zero- and one-dimensional polygon families; the elementary top classes in [F2] are algebraic classes on specified standard diagrams. A cycle representative, if needed, may be selected as the first representative in the explicit enumeration of finite polynomial chains over the countable ring. Nonempty single choices and finite choices require no additional axiom; countably many choices are covered by the assumed Countable Choice.

The geometric generic functions and comparison families can be chosen in the separable smooth spaces on those finitely many compact charts, with their countable derivative seminorms. Their residual conditions are indexed by countable jet charts/exhaustions, the finite singularity types and the countable curve classes; the analytic regularity choices are already furnished by [F4]. For the geometric Baire choices one may recursively select the first basic ball whose closure lies in the preceding ball and in the next dense open set, with diameters tending to zero. Completeness supplies the limit, so this step requires no choice over an uncountable set of functions. Source model relations are imported as finite geometric/count identities, with these actual CC-regular counts; their use does not require a well-ordering of all diagrams or a full-Choice selection of a global transitive system. Consequently the external proof specializes to the declared CC setting. This is a bounded choice inventory of its use here; it is not a claim that the publication itself discusses foundational optimality.

current_manifest_record.statement:
Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element; the sum has one term if the specified structures on the pieces are its restrictions, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For positive-rank triangle pieces choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

derivations.claim: Send the w-regions and z-regions of the given surface to the two colors $U,V$. The source ring is now exactly $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and its variable-power filtration is exactly the specified two-coordinate filtration. The curvature vanishes by the two-color identity. Hence [F1] applies to the actual maps of [F3] as genuine filtered equivariant chain maps, not merely as hat homology maps or uncolored counts.

For different endpoint diagrams first use [F1]'s canonical transition chain-homotopy equivalences to compare maps on the same chosen endpoint representatives. Theorem A then gives a filtered equivariant chain homotopy for any two admitted decompositions and regular auxiliary choices. The source's fourteen Cerf moves include the band, basepoint and quasi-stabilization relations; §12.5 additionally handles components missing one or both ends. Boundary-fixed ambient isotopy preserves the given decorations and induces precisely the required diffeomorphism of decorated cobordisms, so it is covered by the same theorem.

Apply [F2] to the actual gluing and the two specified structures $\mathfrak s_1,\mathfrak s_2$. Restriction of each summand to the two pieces is exactly the condition displayed in the Statement; no unmarked or total-Spin-c map has replaced these maps. The two-color specialization respects the composition and homotopies, giving the displayed formula over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$.

Finally $H^2(S^3\times[0,1];\mathbb Z)=0$ and the product is spin. Its nonempty Spin-c torsor therefore consists of one element. If the chosen structures on the pieces restrict from this unique product structure, the extension set has that one element; otherwise it is empty. In the compatible case the law reduces to ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. The argument imports the established naturality/composition theorems, not an unproved assertion that the local triangle identity checks all movies.

current_manifest_record.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be compact smooth properly embedded oriented surfaces from fixed oriented knots $K_0$ to $K_1$, with the same boundary parametrizations and product collars. Suppose their generic movies represent ambient isotopic cobordisms by an isotopy fixed on those collars. Then one movie can be changed to the other by a finite sequence of planar isotopies, the fifteen Carter–Saito movie moves, sweep-around moves, and interchanges of two disjoint elementary movie events (including disjoint critical points of the surface-height function). A sweep-around moves a closing arc of a one-interval tangle over the tangle to its other side and back underneath, or reverses that movie; geometrically it is a local sheet passage through the missing vertical arc in a spatial chart $S^3\setminus\{\infty\}$. Every intermediate movie represents a generic surface cobordism with the same fixed boundary data.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K_0,K_1\subset S^3$ be smooth oriented knots. A smooth oriented knot cobordism from $K_0$ to $K_1$ is a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ whose boundary is $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$, with product collars at both ends. A **generic movie** for $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing a generic projection of the slices $S^3\times\{t\}$ to the plane and a Morse height function on $\Sigma$, then recording the oriented link diagram at each regular level. Intermediate regular levels may be links with any finite number of components. After choosing the projection and height generically, the finitely many exceptional levels are isolated and distinct: between them the diagrams change by planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, and at them the surface height has one nondegenerate minimum (a birth), one nondegenerate maximum (a death), or one index-one critical point (a saddle band move). A movie includes its ordered list of frames and these elementary changes; no claim that two movies of the same cobordism are equivalent is part of this definition.

Assume countable choice. Fix $\infty\in S^3$, put $A=\{\infty\}\times[0,1]$, and identify its complement with $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$. Let $S_0,S_1$ be compact smooth oriented link cobordisms disjoint from $A$, with the same fixed boundary parametrizations and product collars. If they are ambient isotopic in $S^3\times[0,1]$ relative to those collars, then their comparison factors into finitely many ambient isotopies supported in the Euclidean complement and finitely many local sheet passages through $A$. Each sheet passage occurs at a regular surface-height point and gives the sweep-around move: in planar movies, a closing arc for a one-interval tangle travels over the tangle to the opposite side and returns underneath, or the inverse, retaining its orientation. All end collars remain fixed. No assertion that a sweep-around is generated by the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito moves, or that any homology map respects it, is made.

Assume countable choice. Let two finite generic planar movies represent compact smooth oriented surfaces in $\mathbb R^3\times[0,1]$, with the same parametrized boundary and product collars. If their embedded surfaces are ambient isotopic with compact support relative to those collars, then the two movies are related by a finite sequence of the fifteen Euclidean Carter–Saito local types, distant interchanges of disjoint elementary movie events, and planar isotopies. All orientations and omitted-coordinate crossing orders are retained. This statement concerns Euclidean isotopies; it supplies no sweep-around relation.

Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. current_manifest_record.statement: Assume countable choice. For a smooth oriented knot cobordism in $S^3\times[0,1]$, the ordinary even integral Khovanov assignment has source and target the bigraded groups $Kh^{i,j}$ and is defined up to an overall sign; after quotienting each Khovanov hom-set by the action $f\mapsto -f$, it is invariant under ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary and respects composition. If the surface is equipped with a dividing set and one $w$- and one $z$-basepoint on each boundary knot, the decorated knot Floer assignment has source and target the filtered complexes $CFL^-_{UV}(S^3,K)$ over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$, and is invariant up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. For a general gluing of decorated four-dimensional cobordisms, the link Floer composition law sums over Spin-c structures on the composite that restrict to the chosen structures on the pieces; for the product $S^3\times[0,1]$, this sum has one term if the chosen piece structures are restrictions of the unique product structure, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the law is ordinary composition. The two assignments therefore have separately specified targets, coefficient rings, decorations, and equivalence relations.

citations.quote:
Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented cobordism from an oriented knot $K_0$ to an oriented knot $K_1$, with fixed product collars and fixed endpoint diagrams. Every generic movie $M$ of $\Sigma$ defines a map of bidegree $(0,\chi(\Sigma))$,
$$
Kh(M):Kh^{i,j}(K_0)\longrightarrow Kh^{i,j+\chi(\Sigma)}(K_1),
$$
where $\chi(\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of the surface and the integral even Khovanov groups use the normalized crossing shifts. If two such movies represent cobordisms related by an ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars, their maps differ by multiplication by a single overall sign, independent of the input class. The resulting assignment is a functor after each morphism set is quotiented by the action $f\mapsto -f$; before that quotient the sign is not canonical.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with finite balanced Heegaard data satisfying the strict strong-admissibility condition normalized at all $w$-marks for each specified Spin-c sector. For positive-rank triangle pieces choose the divisor-compatible nearly symmetric regular end paths and generic source-dependent almost-complex perturbations used for the full-marked triangle counts; at rank zero use the empty-product point model. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For an elementary triangle piece with four-dimensional cobordism $W_r$ represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s|_{W_r},\\ n_{w_i}(\phi),n_{z_i}(\phi)\ge0\ \text{for every marked point}}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{\sum_i n_{w_i}(\phi)}V^{\sum_i n_{z_i}(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class on $W_r$, and all marked multiplicities in the sum are nonnegative. The restriction $\mathfrak s|_{W_r}$ is taken under the identification of this elementary cobordism with its Kirby piece. The other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element; the sum has one term if the specified structures on the pieces are its restrictions, and is empty otherwise. In the compatible case the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

derivations.claim: Apply [F1] to the smooth oriented surface. Its target is ordinary even integral $Kh^{i,j}$, and identifying a map with its negative removes exactly the one sign ambiguity. Its isotopy and composition conclusions are the first assertion of the Statement.

For the separately decorated surface apply [F2], coloring all w-regions by $U$ and z-regions by $V$. The intermediate multiply based link modules and their endpoint naturality identifications are part of that construction. Zero curvature makes the endpoint objects the specified complexes, and external Theorem A gives filtered equivariant chain-homotopy invariance. This assertion has coefficient field $\mathbb F_2$ and its own decoration and Spin-c data; no integral Khovanov sign ambiguity or comparison between the two theories is transferred to it.

The general composition law is the extension sum in [F2]. On $S^3\times[0,1]$ the Spin-c set has one element, so the extension sum is a singleton for compatible piece structures and empty otherwise. Combining the two independently established assignments proves the entire Statement with its distinct targets, coefficients and equivalence relations. It asserts neither equality of the functors nor a canonical chain-level top generator, and requires no new local reconstruction of the imported Cerf checks.

citations.quote: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and let $(M,\gamma)$ be the balanced sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact exterior of $K$ along $F$. For a surface-adapted admissible sutured Heegaard diagram, the generator correspondence between the top Alexander summand of the knot Floer complex and the sutured Floer disk-count module identifies their disk-count differentials. Under the hypotheses of a horizontal decomposition, the induced chain map realizes Ni's horizontal decomposition formula. For an essential separating product annulus with connected $R_+$ and $R_-$ whose decomposition has two balanced pieces, the induced chain map realizes Ni's product-annulus tensor formula. These assertions use the specified basepoint domains, periodic-domain admissibility, and exact characteristic-product-region hypotheses; they make no claim that generic Heegaard disk existence alone supplies the decomposition maps.

derivations.claim: Let $E$ be the compact exterior and $(M,\gamma)$ its cut along $F$. Its two faces are copies of $F$, and its vertical boundary is the annulus $\partial F\times I$. It is balanced: both faces have Euler characteristic $1-2g$, no component is closed, and every boundary component meets the vertical annulus. A meridian intersects $F$ algebraically once, so $F$ is nonseparating and the cut is connected.

The signed cut comparison gives $\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)\cong\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. The grading uses the supplied class $[F]$ and genus of this actual surface; no genus-detection theorem for a different ambient manifold is substituted.

The irreducibility assumption applies to $E$: pushing away the deleted-knot end identifies every compact sphere question with that in $Y\setminus K$. A sphere in the interior of $M$ is therefore a sphere disjoint from $F$ in $E$ and bounds a ball in $E$. Since $F$ is connected and disjoint from this sphere, if it entered the ball it would lie wholly in its interior, contradicting $\partial F\subset\partial E$. The ball is consequently disjoint from $F$; shrink the cut collar if necessary to obtain the same ball in $M$. Thus $M$ is irreducible.

If $(M,\gamma)$ were not taut, its integral sutured Floer homology would vanish by the external vanishing input, contradicting step 1.2. Therefore it is taut. This is the contrapositive of F2, not a reversal of taut hierarchy nonvanishing.

If the taut balanced $(M,\gamma)$ were not a product, F3 would give $\mathbb Z^2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$. Such an injection into $\mathbb Z$ is impossible: images $a,b$ of its two basis vectors satisfy the nontrivial integer relation $b a-a b=0$ when either is nonzero, and an image zero itself contradicts injectivity. The two disjoint outer summands in the source argument therefore contradict step 1.2. Hence the actual $F$-cut exterior is a product sutured manifold. This includes $g=0$ and uses the corrected characteristic-pair qualification F4.

citations.quote: Let a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented three-manifold be fibered with a specified connected oriented Seifert fiber. Its compact exterior with two meridional sutures admits a good surface-adapted balanced diagram carrying that actual Seifert surface, its boundary longitude, and the meridional boundary trivialization. For a fiber of an actual open book the cut/double diagram represents the marked product obtained by cutting along the fiber, with the original monodromy retained in regluing.

A good admissible surface-adapted balanced diagram can be made nice by a finite sequence of permissible fingers and own-family disk slides preserving its surface marking. Weak admissibility is preserved. Every complementary region of the underlying diagram disjoint from its true boundary is a bigon or square.

Two balanced Heegaard diagrams of the same marked sutured manifold are connected by relative attaching-circle isotopies, own-family disk slides, and ordinary stabilizations and destabilizations. An ordinary stabilization can be moved by such slides to the true boundary region. These moves induce integral chain homotopy equivalences for the transported coherent orientation class. The product sutured manifold has integral homology equal to one copy of the integers; on a homology-product branch the periodic-domain character ambiguity vanishes.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

For an actual nice admissible good surface diagram whose cut has zero periodic-domain group, the outer differential and the cut differential are identified over the integers after changing generator signs. This identifies the top Alexander homology with the integral homology of the cut diagram when the surface is the marked Seifert surface and the outer degree is its genus. The conclusion applies in particular to a fiber cut and to the rank-one branch of the cut Euler-matrix reduction.

Signed relative diagram moves compare the resulting complex to the chosen defining complex, with its specified coherent orientation class transported. No restriction on Y or change of coefficient ring is made.

In this marked adapted diagram the local Euler obstruction is minus 2g plus twice the number of interior polygon coordinates when evaluated on minus F. Therefore the Alexander degree is g minus that number: degree g is precisely the outer generator set, and no higher degree occurs. The product cut has zero periodic-domain group, either directly from its empty product diagram and the relative handle description, or from its vanishing relative integral homology. The signed cut comparison consequently identifies the whole degree-g differential with the cut differential, after harmless changes of generator signs.

The empty diagram of the actual product has one empty-tuple generator and no nonconstant disk, so its integral chain complex is Z with zero differential. The signed relative move equivalences identify its homology with that of the actual cut diagram. Combining with the full top-summand chain identification gives the asserted integral group isomorphism. The exterior orientation character restricts trivially to the zero-periodic cut, so this conclusion holds for the specified defining class without asserting equivalence of arbitrary orientation systems on the uncut exterior.
